Accountable obligation owner.value: Responsible Actuary (hoken keirinin) designated under IBA Art. 120 owns the policy-reserve calculation for the 31 March business year end; the Chief Actuary approves any change to the statement of calculation methods

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IBA Art. 116 and Ordinance for Enforcement Arts. 68-69 re-read at each valuation date, together with the standard yield rate notification (FSA Notification 1996 No. 48) and the standard mortality tables (Standard Life Table 2018 for death protection, 2007 post-annuitisation table, 2018 third-sector table) in force for each issue-year cohort

In-scope processes.value: Statutory policy-reserve valuation at 31 March year end and at the June/September/December quarter ends, covering premium reserve, unearned premium reserve, refund reserve and contingency reserves I/II/III for all in-force individual life, annuity, group and third-sector blocks plus variable annuity minimum-guarantee reserves

In-scope systems.value: Prophet statutory valuation libraries fed by the policy administration in-force extract; run outputs posted to the statutory ledger and stored against a locked run id

Compliance procedure documented.value: Statutory Policy Reserve Valuation Procedure (Japan) — cohort split at the 1 April 1996 standard-reserve boundary, net level premium method, standard basis lookup by issue year, contingency reserve I/II/III build, surrender-value floor test and additional policy reserve test

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Actuary and countersigned by the CFO; re-approved whenever the statement of calculation methods (santei hoho sho) is amended under IBA Art. 123 or a new FSA notification changes the standard yield rate or mortality table

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Year-end reserve locked at the 31 March ledger close and feeds the Art. 110 business report due to the FSA within 3 months of business year end (30 June); each quarterly valuation closes within 30 days of quarter end

Deadline reminders configured.value: Valuation calendar milestones alert the actuarial team at extract cut (year end + 3 business days), model run complete (+10), peer review cleared (+15) and ledger post (+20), with a 15 June alert for the business-report reserve schedules

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Valuation workpapers, run logs, basis tables, model point files and GL reconciliations retained 10 years from the business year end in the compliance evidence repository, indexed by run id and business year

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Reserve shortfalls, wrong-cohort basis application, failed surrender-value floor tests and post-close adjustments logged with root cause, yen impact and the corrected reserve amount

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Chief Actuary signs off every basis correction and every restatement of a booked policy reserve before it is posted

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every in-force cohort valued at 31 March — by product code, issue-year band, reserve component and pre/post 1 April 1996 standard-reserve status — as listed in the locked valuation run output

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Recomputed reserve must fall within 0.05% of the booked reserve for each sampled cohort; any cohort valued on the wrong standard yield rate or mortality table, or any reserve below the contract's surrender value floor, is an automatic fail regardless of size

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual at 31 March with quarterly interim valuations; the full recomputation test runs on the year-end valuation, with a reduced movement-and-basis-control test each quarter

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have built, parameterised or run any sampled valuation model version

Evidence location for test results.value: Year-end policy reserve validation workpaper (population extract, cohort sample, seriatim recomputation, exception log) filed in the model governance repository against the locked valuation run id

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Basis tables by issue-year cohort, cohort-to-GL reconciliation and the seriatim recomputation pack, producible for an FSA on-site inspection or a Responsible Actuary follow-up within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Appointed Actuary answers FSA valuation questions through Regulatory Reporting as the single channel; Regulatory Counsel clears any statement that admits a reserve restatement before it leaves the company

checklist.step: Freeze the valuation date and confirm the calculation basis in force
actions: Open the filed statement of calculation methods (santei hoho sho) held with the basic documents and confirm the version number and FSA acceptance date that governs the 31 March valuation.
Ask the Regulatory Reporting Manager whether any Art. 123 amendment to the calculation methods was submitted during the business year and, if so, from which contract date it applies.
Record the valuation date, the business year, and the applicable notification versions for the standard yield rate and each standard mortality table on the valuation control sheet.
Circulate the control sheet to the Chief Actuary and the Controller so the close calendar and the ledger cut-off are set to the same date.
checklist.done: the valuation control sheet names the governing calculation-methods version, the valuation date and every standard-basis notification version, and is acknowledged by the Chief Actuary.

checklist.step: Pull the in-force extract from the policy administration system
actions: Run the statutory valuation extract job for the 31 March position, selecting all contracts with status In Force, Paid-Up, Extended Term, Disability Waiver and Annuity In Payment.

Include on every record: policy number, plan code, issue date, entry age, sex, premium paying term, policy term, sum assured, annuity amount, mode and modal premium, last premium due date, rider codes, fund values for variable contracts and the guaranteed minimum benefit type.
Produce the extract control totals (record count, total sum assured, total annualised premium, total account value) and sign them into the extract control sheet.
Hand the extract and control totals to the Reserving Actuary through the actuarial data landing zone, not by email attachment.
checklist.done: a dated in-force extract with signed control totals is delivered to actuarial and its record count ties to the policy admin in-force count at 31 March.

checklist.step: Split the in-force into standard-reserve and non-standard cohorts
actions: Tag every contract with a contract date on or after 1 April 1996 in a covered product class as STANDARD (standard policy reserve under Enforcement Regulation Art. 68).
Tag pre-1996 contracts and product classes outside the standard-reserve scope as COMPANY BASIS, valued on the method written in the statement of calculation methods.
List the exception classes separately — variable products, foreign-currency contracts, group annuity blocks and reinsurance-ceded business — because each takes a different reserve rule.
Reconcile the sum of the cohort counts back to the extract record count and investigate any contract that lands in no cohort.
checklist.done: every extracted contract sits in exactly one cohort, the cohort counts sum to the extract record count, and the cohort rule applied is written on each cohort row.

checklist.step: Load the standard yield rate and standard mortality table for each cohort
actions: For each STANDARD cohort look up the standard yield rate applicable to its contract-date band and premium type (level vs single premium, yen vs foreign currency) in FSA Notification 1996 No. 48 as amended.

Attach the standard mortality table matching the benefit type: Standard Life Table 2018 for death protection, the post-annuitisation standard table for annuities in payment, and the 2018 third-sector table for medical and cancer riders.
Enter each rate and table id into the model basis table and have a second actuarial analyst independently key the same values into a comparison sheet.
Resolve every difference between the two keyings before the run is released; a single mis-keyed rate mis-states an entire issue-year cohort.
checklist.done: each cohort carries a documented standard yield rate and mortality table id, double-keyed and reconciled with zero unresolved differences.

checklist.step: Validate the model points against the source extract
actions: Run the model point build and compare its output totals (count, sum assured, annualised premium, account value) to the signed extract control totals line by line.

Investigate every field-level rejection in the build log — missing entry age, unmapped plan code, issue date after the valuation date — and clear them with the Policy Administration Analyst rather than dropping the record.
Confirm no contract was silently defaulted: check the model's default-applied counter is zero for entry age, sex, term and premium term.
Save the build log and the tie-out sheet against the run id in the model governance repository.
checklist.done: model point totals tie to the signed extract control totals within rounding, and the build log shows zero dropped and zero defaulted records.

checklist.step: Run the premium reserve on the net level premium method
actions: Execute the statutory valuation run for STANDARD cohorts on the net level premium method prescribed by Enforcement Regulation Art. 68, using the loaded standard yield rate and mortality table.
Execute the COMPANY BASIS cohorts on the method and assumptions written in the filed statement of calculation methods, quoting the clause reference in the run header.
Lock the run and record the run id, model version, basis table version and executing user in the run register.
Export the premium reserve by product, issue-year band and cohort into the reserve summary workbook.
checklist.done: a locked run produces premium reserve by product and issue-year cohort, with the method for every cohort traceable to either Art. 68 or a named clause of the calculation-methods statement.

checklist.step: Value the unearned premium reserve and the refund reserve
actions: Compute the unearned premium reserve for the unexpired portion of premiums received before 31 March, using the modal premium and the last premium due date on each model point.
Compute the refund reserve for accumulated dividends, deferred refunds and policyholder dividend reserve balances taken from the policy administration dividend module.
Agree the dividend reserve balance with the Controller's dividend liability account before it enters the reserve summary.
Add both components to the reserve summary workbook as separate lines under the Art. 116 policy reserve total, never netted into the premium reserve.
checklist.done: unearned premium reserve and refund reserve appear as separate, source-agreed lines in the reserve summary and the dividend element ties to the Controller's balance.

checklist.step: Build contingency reserves I, II and III
actions: Compute contingency reserve I for insurance risk on the accumulation rates and risk bases set by the Enforcement Regulation and the supporting FSA notification, applied to the relevant risk exposure measure per product group.

Compute contingency reserve II for assumed-interest-rate risk against the guaranteed rate blocks, and contingency reserve III for the minimum guarantee risk on variable annuity and variable life business.

For variable annuity minimum guarantees, state whether the standard method or an approved alternative method is used and reference the approval; run the scenario set the method requires and record the resulting reserve.
Compare each contingency reserve against its prescribed accumulation limit and record whether the year's accumulation is capped.
Where a drawdown is proposed, document the qualifying loss event and get the Chief Actuary's written approval before it is reflected.
checklist.done: contingency reserves I, II and III are computed, tested against their limits, and any drawdown carries a documented qualifying event and Chief Actuary approval.

checklist.step: Test the surrender value floor and the need for an additional policy reserve
actions: For every model point compare the computed reserve to the contract's surrender value at 31 March and set the reserve to the higher of the two where the floor bites.
List the legacy high-guarantee blocks (contracts issued in the high assumed-rate era) and project their future cash flows against the current expected investment yield.
Where the projection shows the existing reserve insufficient, quantify the additional policy reserve required and the funding schedule over the permitted accumulation period.
Take the additional reserve proposal, with the projection assumptions, to the Chief Actuary and the CFO for decision before year-end close.
checklist.done: every model point satisfies the surrender value floor and any additional policy reserve is quantified, scheduled and approved before the ledger close.

checklist.step: Analyse the reserve movement from the prior valuation
actions: Build an analysis of change from the 31 March prior-year reserve to this year's: new business, premium accrual and interest accretion, deaths, surrenders and lapses, maturities and annuitisations, basis changes and model changes.
Require each step to be explained in yen and as a percentage of the opening reserve; leave no unexplained residual above 0.1% of the opening reserve.
Attribute any basis-change step to the specific notification or calculation-methods amendment that caused it.
Present the analysis to the Chief Actuary with the largest three movements narrated in plain language.
checklist.done: the analysis of change reconciles opening to closing reserve with every step attributed and no unexplained residual above 0.1% of the opening reserve.

checklist.step: Peer review the valuation run and clear the review points
actions: Assign a reviewing actuary who did not run the valuation and give them the run id, basis tables, model point tie-out and analysis of change.
Have the reviewer re-perform a spot recomputation on at least one model point per product group by hand or in an independent spreadsheet.
Log every review point with a severity, an owner and a due date; block the ledger post until all high-severity points are closed.
Record the reviewer's name, date and conclusion against the run id in the model governance repository.
checklist.done: a named independent reviewer has signed the run with all high-severity review points closed and spot recomputations documented.

checklist.step: Post the policy reserve to the statutory ledger and reconcile
actions: Post the reserve journal by component — premium reserve, unearned premium reserve, refund reserve, contingency reserves I/II/III, additional policy reserve — to the mapped statutory liability accounts.
Reconcile the posted total to the reserve summary workbook and the locked run output, and attach the reconciliation to the journal in the ledger.
Ask the Controller to confirm the reserve movement flows correctly through the profit and loss statement for the business year.
Freeze the accounts once agreed and mark the run id as the reporting run of record for the business year.
checklist.done: posted ledger balances equal the locked valuation run output by component, with the reconciliation attached to the journal and the run marked as the run of record.

checklist.step: Prepare the reserve schedules for the Art. 110 business report
actions: Populate the policy reserve schedules of the business report in the FSA-prescribed layout: reserve by insurance class, by reserve component, and the standard vs non-standard split.
Tie every schedule cell to a line of the reserve summary workbook and record the cell-to-source map alongside the draft.
Send the draft schedules to the Appointed Actuary for confirmation that they match the valuation on which the actuarial opinion will be given.
Hold the schedules in the reporting pack for submission within 3 months of the 31 March business year end (by 30 June).
checklist.done: business report reserve schedules are populated, source-mapped cell by cell and confirmed by the Appointed Actuary ahead of the 30 June submission window.

checklist.step: Document the basis and method in the valuation report
actions: Write the valuation report covering scope, data, cohort rules, standard basis by issue-year band, methods applied for non-standard business, contingency reserves and the additional reserve decision.
State explicitly where the valuation followed the filed calculation-methods statement and where the standard basis under Enforcement Regulation Art. 68 overrode it.
Attach the run register entry, basis tables, model point tie-out, analysis of change and peer review sign-off as numbered appendices.
Sign and date the report and register it as the source document for the Art. 121 actuarial opinion.
checklist.done: a signed, appendix-complete valuation report exists and is registered as the source for the actuarial opinion.

checklist.step: Retain the valuation evidence for the retention period
actions: Move the full valuation folder — extract, control totals, basis tables, run logs, reserve summary, analysis of change, peer review, GL reconciliation and signed report — into the evidence repository under business year and run id.
Apply the 10-year retention label so the record survives system replacement and product wind-down.
Confirm the repository index makes the record searchable by business year, product class and run id.
Record the storage location on the valuation control sheet so an FSA inspector can be pointed at it in one step.
checklist.done: the complete valuation folder is stored under a 10-year retention label and retrievable by business year, product class and run id.

testing.step: Build the population of valued cohorts from the run of record
actions: Take the locked 31 March run of record and export every cohort row: product code, issue-year band, standard vs company basis flag, contract count, reserve by component.
Confirm with the Reserving Actuary that no cohort was valued outside this run or adjusted manually after the lock.
Add any manual post-close adjustment journals from the ledger as separate population rows so top-side entries cannot hide.
Sign the population as complete and date it before drawing any sample.
testing.done: the cohort population is exported from the locked run, includes every manual adjustment, and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the policy admin in-force and the general ledger
actions: Compare the population contract count and sum assured to the policy administration in-force report at 31 March and explain every difference in units, not percentages.
Compare the population reserve total by component to the posted statutory liability account balances.
Trace each reconciling item to a documented cause — reinsurance ceded, contracts in suspense, currency translation — and reject any that is only labelled 'timing'.
Record the three-way reconciliation (run, policy admin, ledger) in the workpaper with sign-off from the extractor.
testing.done: run, policy admin and ledger agree, with every reconciling item explained by a named documented cause.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of cohorts and seriatim policies
actions: Take 100% of cohorts whose reserve exceeds 5% of the total policy reserve and 100% of variable annuity minimum-guarantee cohorts.
Take 25 further cohorts by seeded random selection from the remainder, and within each sampled cohort select 3 policies at random for seriatim recomputation.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and selection rule so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Confirm the sample covers both pre-1996 company-basis and post-1996 standard-basis contracts.
testing.done: a reproducible sample is drawn covering all material and variable-annuity cohorts plus both basis populations, with the seed recorded.

testing.step: Re-perform the standard basis lookup for each sampled cohort
actions: For each sampled cohort read the contract-date band and independently look up the standard yield rate in FSA Notification 1996 No. 48 as it stood at the contract date.
Independently select the mortality table the benefit type requires (Standard Life Table 2018, post-annuitisation table, 2018 third-sector table) before looking at the model basis table.
Compare your conclusion to the basis table loaded in the run; any difference in rate or table id is an exception, including a right rate cited to the wrong notification.
Capture the notification page relied on into the workpaper with the date of access.
testing.done: each sampled cohort has an independent basis conclusion, compared to the model and evidenced by a dated source capture.

testing.step: Independently recompute reserves for the sampled seriatim policies
actions: Rebuild the net level premium reserve for each sampled policy in an independent spreadsheet from entry age, sex, term, premium term, sum assured and the independently selected basis.
Compare the recomputed reserve to the run output and express the difference in yen and as a percentage of the booked reserve.
Flag any policy outside the 0.05% tolerance and trace the cause to data, basis or method before calling it an exception.
For company-basis policies re-perform against the clause of the calculation-methods statement, not against Art. 68.
testing.done: every sampled policy is recomputed independently and each difference outside 0.05% is traced to a named cause.

testing.step: Verify the contingency reserve and minimum guarantee computations
actions: Recompute contingency reserve I and II on the prescribed accumulation rates applied to the exposure measures in the run output and compare to the booked amounts.
For contingency reserve III confirm the method used for variable annuity minimum guarantees matches the approved method and that the required scenario set was actually run.
Test each reserve against its prescribed accumulation limit and confirm that any capped year is disclosed in the valuation report.
Where a drawdown occurred, verify the qualifying loss event and the Chief Actuary approval both pre-date the posting.
testing.done: contingency reserves I, II and III recompute within tolerance and every cap or drawdown is supported by approval and disclosure.

testing.step: Re-perform the surrender value floor and additional reserve tests
actions: For every sampled policy pull the surrender value from the policy administration system at 31 March and compare it to the booked reserve.
List any policy where the booked reserve is below the surrender value; this is a breach, not a tolerance item.
For the legacy high-guarantee blocks re-run the sufficiency projection at the stated expected yield and compare the additional reserve conclusion to the one booked.
Confirm the additional reserve funding schedule matches the schedule approved by the Chief Actuary and CFO.
testing.done: no sampled policy is reserved below its surrender value and the additional reserve conclusion and funding schedule are independently confirmed.

testing.step: Trace booked reserves through to the business report schedules
actions: Take each policy reserve schedule cell in the draft business report and follow the cell-to-source map back to the reserve summary and the run output.
Confirm the standard versus non-standard split in the schedule matches the cohort tagging in the run.
Check the schedule totals equal the posted ledger balances and that the submission is dated within 3 months of the 31 March business year end.
Capture the traced schedule pages into the workpaper.
testing.done: every reserve schedule cell traces to the run of record and the schedule totals equal the ledger, ahead of the 30 June submission deadline.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception recording cohort, policy numbers, yen impact and which of Art. 116, Art. 68 or the calculation-methods statement was not met.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list — extract data defect, wrong basis loaded, model coding, manual adjustment, method not per filed document — and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date inside the next quarterly valuation cycle and, for any reserve shortfall, open an assessment with Regulatory Counsel on whether an FSA notification is required.
Carry every open exception into the next valuation test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, a yen impact, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate by cohort and by yen exposure and compare it to the 0.05% recomputation tolerance and the zero-tolerance basis and floor criteria.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references that support it.
Have the independent reviewer, who built and ran none of the sampled models, sign the workpaper with name and date.
Report the conclusion and any reserve shortfall to the Chief Actuary and the Audit Committee at their next sitting and file the workpaper against the run id.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and reporting date is filed against the valuation run of record.

checklist.step: Confirm the Responsible Actuary appointment is current and recorded
actions: Retrieve the board resolution appointing the Responsible Actuary under IBA Art. 120 and confirm it names the individual who will sign this year's opinion.
Confirm the appointment notification was filed with the FSA and that any change of holder during the business year was notified when it happened.
Check the appointee still meets the qualification requirements (Institute of Actuaries of Japan membership and required years of practical experience) and file the current membership evidence.
Record the appointment reference on the opinion control sheet that will travel with this year's opinion file.
checklist.done: a current board resolution, an FSA notification reference and current qualification evidence exist for the individual who will sign the opinion.

checklist.step: Fix the confirmation scope for the business year
actions: List each matter the Responsible Actuary must confirm under IBA Art. 121 and the Cabinet Office Ordinance: adequacy of policy reserves, fairness of the policyholder dividend allocation, and the further prescribed items.
For each matter name the workpaper that will support it and the actuary who will prepare it.
Confirm with the Regulatory Reporting Manager that no additional confirmation item was added by an FSA supervisory notice during the year.
Circulate the scope sheet to the Chief Actuary and the Audit Committee secretary before fieldwork starts.
checklist.done: every confirmation item has a named supporting workpaper and preparer, agreed with the Chief Actuary before fieldwork.

checklist.step: Adopt the practice standard edition and record any departure
actions: Record the edition and issue date of the Institute of Actuaries of Japan practice standard for the Responsible Actuary that applies to this business year.
Read the year's revisions and list, item by item, what changes in the analysis compared with last year.
Where the company departs from a standard treatment, write the departure, the reason and the effect on the conclusion; a departure without a written rationale cannot be carried into the opinion.
Have the Chief Actuary countersign the adoption and departure record.
checklist.done: the applicable practice standard edition is recorded, its revisions assessed, and every departure is written up and countersigned.

checklist.step: Assemble the source valuation evidence for the confirmation
actions: Pull the signed valuation report for the 31 March run of record together with its basis tables, model point tie-out, analysis of change and peer review sign-off.
Confirm the valuation run id in the evidence pack is the same run posted to the statutory ledger, not a later re-run.
Obtain the Controller's confirmation that the reserve balances in the draft financial statements equal that run.
Index the pack as Appendix A of the opinion file so each confirmation statement can cite a page.
checklist.done: the opinion file holds the signed valuation report for the run of record, agreed to the draft financial statements by the Controller.

checklist.step: Design the future cash-flow analysis scenarios
actions: Set the projection period and the base scenario assumptions: expected investment yield by asset class from the Chief Investment Officer, mortality and morbidity from recent experience studies, lapse rates by product and duration, and expense unit costs from the Controller.

Build the stress scenarios the practice standard requires — sustained low interest rates, an adverse mortality or morbidity shock, elevated lapse on high-guarantee blocks, and an equity fall for variable annuity guarantees.
Document the source of every assumption on the assumption schedule with the date and the person who provided it; no assumption may be sourced to 'management judgement' alone.
Have the Model Risk Manager review the scenario design before the runs are executed.
checklist.done: base and required stress scenarios are defined with every assumption source-attributed and the design reviewed by Model Risk before execution.

checklist.step: Run the future cash-flow analysis and grade it against the continuation criteria
actions: Execute each scenario on the locked year-end model and export the projected policy reserve, projected net assets and projected solvency margin ratio for every projection year.
Apply the continuation criteria in the practice standard — the projected solvency margin ratio must not fall below the prescribed sound-management level during the projection period.
Grade each scenario pass or fail against the criteria and list the projection years and the yen shortfall for any failure.
Where a scenario fails, quantify the management actions available (additional policy reserve funding, asset reallocation, new business repricing) and their effect when re-run.
checklist.done: every scenario is executed, graded against the continuation criteria, and each failure is quantified with a modelled management action.

checklist.step: Test the fairness of the policyholder dividend allocation
actions: Obtain from the Controller the year's divisible surplus by participating block and the dividend amounts credited by product and issue-year cohort.
Re-perform the allocation on the contribution principle stated in the filed calculation-methods statement — mortality, interest and expense sources by cohort.
Compare credited dividends between cohorts of similar experience and investigate any cohort receiving materially more or less than its contribution supports.
Write the conclusion on fairness and equity, naming any cohort that required an explanation and how it was resolved.
checklist.done: the dividend allocation is re-performed by contribution source with a written fairness conclusion covering every participating cohort.

checklist.step: Check the valuation against the filed basic documents
actions: Read the filed statement of calculation methods clause by clause and mark each clause as applied, superseded by the standard basis, or not applicable this year.
List any product valued on a method that no clause supports and treat it as a potential IBA Art. 4(2) inconsistency, not an actuarial preference.
Ask Regulatory Counsel whether any such inconsistency requires an Art. 123 amendment filing before the opinion is signed.
Record the clause-by-clause mark-up as an appendix to the attached report.
checklist.done: every clause of the filed calculation-methods statement is marked up and any unsupported method has a documented counsel position.

checklist.step: Draft the written opinion with the prescribed confirmation wording
actions: Draft the opinion covering each Art. 121 confirmation item in turn, stating the conclusion in the wording the practice standard prescribes.
Choose the opinion form deliberately — unqualified, qualified, or adverse — and where it is not unqualified state the matter, its yen effect and what management must do.
Reference the supporting workpaper and appendix page behind every confirmation statement so no sentence stands unsupported.
Leave the signature block, the date and the Institute of Actuaries of Japan membership number to be completed only after board presentation.
checklist.done: a complete draft opinion exists in which every confirmation statement cites its supporting appendix and the opinion form is deliberately chosen.

checklist.step: Draft the attached report supporting the opinion
actions: Write the attached report covering data and its validation, reserve method and basis by cohort, the future cash-flow analysis design, scenario results and continuation grading, the dividend fairness test and the additional policy reserve position.
Include the assumption schedule with sources and the sensitivity of the conclusion to the two assumptions with the largest effect.
Show the prior-year comparatives for each scenario so a reviewer can see the direction of travel.
Circulate the draft to the Chief Actuary and the ALM actuary for technical comment and resolve each comment in writing.
checklist.done: the attached report is complete with assumption sources, sensitivities and prior-year comparatives, and all technical comments are resolved in writing.

checklist.step: Run the independent technical review of the opinion package
actions: Assign a reviewer who contributed nothing to the valuation, the scenarios or the drafting.
Have the reviewer re-trace three confirmation statements to their workpapers and re-run one stress scenario from the assumption schedule.
Log review points with severity and owner; no high-severity point may remain open when the opinion is signed.
Record the reviewer name, date and conclusion in the model governance repository against the opinion file reference.
checklist.done: an independent reviewer has re-traced sampled statements and re-run a scenario, with all high-severity points closed before signature.

checklist.step: Obtain legal review of the opinion wording
actions: Review the opinion against IBA Art. 121 to confirm each required confirmation is actually made and none is answered by implication.
Where the opinion is qualified or adverse, advise on the disclosure consequences in the business report and on whether a prior FSA conversation is advisable.
Confirm nothing in the opinion contradicts the filed basic documents or the draft financial statements.
Record the legal clearance with date and reviewer in the matter file and attach it to the opinion control sheet.
checklist.done: legal clearance is recorded, confirming every Art. 121 confirmation is expressly made and any qualification has an agreed disclosure treatment.

checklist.step: Present the opinion to the board of directors
actions: Place the opinion and the attached report on the agenda of the board meeting that approves the 31 March financial statements, and load them to the board portal by the pack cut-off.
Have the Responsible Actuary present the conclusion in person, including any qualification and the management actions modelled.
Ensure the minutes record the date, the presentation, the directors present, the questions raised and the board's acknowledgement or resolution.
Issue a certified minute extract naming the presentation date — this is the date from which the without-delay submission clock runs.
checklist.done: the board minutes record the presentation date and the board's acknowledgement, and a certified extract is issued to the opinion file.

checklist.step: Sign the opinion and release it for submission to the FSA
actions: Complete the signature block with name, seal, Institute of Actuaries of Japan membership number and the signature date, which must not pre-date the board presentation.
Register the signed opinion and attached report in the evidence repository and lock them against further edit.
Hand the signed set to the Regulatory Reporting Manager with the certified board minute extract and the target submission date of board date plus 5 business days.
Record the handover on the opinion control sheet with time and recipient.
checklist.done: the opinion is signed, dated on or after the board presentation, locked in the repository and formally handed to Regulatory Reporting with the submission clock stated.

checklist.step: Retain the opinion evidence and index it for an Art. 122 request
actions: File the opinion, attached report, scenario files, assumption schedule, dividend workpaper, review records, legal clearance and board minute extract as one indexed folder under the business year.
Apply the 10-year retention label and confirm the folder is searchable by business year, Responsible Actuary name and opinion form.
Prepare a one-page index that maps each Art. 121 confirmation to its supporting document and page so an Art. 122 explanation request can be answered in 5 business days.
Give the index location to the Regulatory Reporting Manager and the General Counsel.
checklist.done: the full opinion folder is retained for 10 years with a confirmation-to-evidence index lodged with Regulatory Reporting and Legal.

testing.step: Build the population of assertions made in the opinion
actions: Read the signed opinion and the attached report and list every confirmation, conclusion and quantitative assertion as a separate population row.
Add each scenario the practice standard requires as a row, whether or not it appears in the report, so an omitted scenario shows as a gap.
Confirm with the Appointed Actuary that no assertion was added or removed after the board pack was cut.
Sign and date the assertion population before testing begins.
testing.done: a signed population lists every assertion in the opinion plus every practice-standard scenario, including any that is missing.

testing.step: Reconcile the opinion to the valuation run of record and the financial statements
actions: Compare every reserve figure quoted in the opinion and attached report to the locked valuation run output and the posted statutory ledger balances.
Confirm the run id referenced in the opinion is the run posted to the ledger and not a later re-run.
Compare the solvency margin ratio quoted in the report to the ratio in the regulatory return for the same date.
List every difference in yen and require a documented explanation before sampling.
testing.done: every figure in the opinion ties to the run of record, the ledger and the solvency return, with all differences explained.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of assertions and scenarios
actions: Take 100% of the Art. 121 confirmation statements and 100% of any qualification wording.
Take a seeded random sample of 10 supporting quantitative assertions from the attached report plus 2 stress scenarios for re-execution.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and rule so the sample is reproducible.
Confirm the sample includes at least one assertion relating to dividend fairness and one to the additional policy reserve.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all confirmation statements, sampled quantitative assertions and two scenarios for re-execution.

testing.step: Re-trace each confirmation statement to its supporting workpaper
actions: For each confirmation statement open the cited appendix and page and read whether it actually supports the words used.
Treat a citation that points at a folder rather than a page, or at a workpaper prepared after the signature date, as an exception.
Check that the practice standard edition cited in the opinion is the edition in force for the business year.
Capture the cited pages into the workpaper with their document versions.
testing.done: every confirmation statement is supported by a specific, pre-dated, correctly versioned workpaper page captured into the test file.

testing.step: Re-execute sampled stress scenarios from the assumption schedule
actions: Rebuild the sampled scenarios from the documented assumption schedule without reference to the original run settings.
Compare the projected reserve, net assets and solvency margin ratio path to the reported results year by year.
Investigate any difference above 1% of projected net assets and identify whether the assumption schedule or the executed run is wrong.
Confirm the continuation-criteria grading follows from the numbers rather than from a narrative conclusion.
testing.done: sampled scenarios reproduce within 1% of projected net assets and the continuation grading follows arithmetically from the results.

testing.step: Re-perform the dividend fairness test on selected cohorts
actions: Select three participating cohorts, pull their divisible surplus contribution by mortality, interest and expense source from the Controller's schedules.
Recompute the dividend that the contribution principle in the filed calculation-methods statement produces and compare it to the amount credited.
Investigate any cohort whose credited dividend departs from its contribution by more than the tolerance stated in the fairness workpaper.
Confirm the fairness conclusion in the opinion is consistent with what the recomputation shows.
testing.done: recomputed dividends for the selected cohorts support the fairness conclusion, or the departure is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Verify the board presentation and the submission clock
actions: Read the board minutes for the meeting that approved the financial statements and confirm the opinion was presented and acknowledged, with directors named.
Compare the opinion signature date to the board presentation date; a signature that pre-dates the presentation is an exception.
Compute the elapsed business days from the board presentation date to the FSA submission timestamp and compare to the without-delay standard and the 5-business-day internal service level.
Capture the minute extract and the submission receipt into the workpaper.
testing.done: the minutes evidence presentation, the signature post-dates it, and the elapsed days to FSA submission are computed and within the stated standard.

testing.step: Test the practice standard departures and any qualification
actions: Read the departure record against the practice standard edition in force and confirm each departure has a reason and an assessed effect on the conclusion.

Where the opinion is qualified or adverse, confirm the same matter is disclosed in the business report and that the modelled management action is actually committed by management, with an owner and a date.
Confirm the legal clearance pre-dates the signature and covers the final wording, not an earlier draft.
Flag any departure that materially changes the conclusion but was not brought to the board.
testing.done: every departure and qualification is reasoned, disclosed consistently and cleared by legal before signature, with board visibility evidenced.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the confirmation item, the missing or contradicted support and the Art. 121 duty affected.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list — workpaper not produced, scenario omitted, wording unsupported, late board tabling, late submission — and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date ahead of the next business year's cash-flow analysis kick-off.
Where the FSA submission was late, open an assessment with the General Counsel on self-reporting and record the decision and its reason.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and, for late submission, a documented self-report decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report to the Audit Committee
actions: Compute the number of unsupported assertions and omitted scenarios against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer from outside the actuarial function sign the workpaper with name and date.
Report the conclusion to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper under the business year alongside the signed opinion.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion and exception count and is reported to the Audit Committee and filed with the opinion.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual submission package to the FSA / competent Local Finance Bureau — business report, financial statements and the Responsible Actuary opinion — and the basic-documents consistency check behind it

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IBA Art. 4 and Art. 4(2) (basic documents: articles of incorporation, statement of business procedures, general policy conditions, statement of calculation methods), Art. 123 (amendment of basic documents) and Art. 121(3) (submission of the actuarial opinion without delay), read with the Ordinance for Enforcement submission forms in force for the business year

In-scope processes.value: Annual regulatory submission for the 31 March business year — assembly, basic-documents consistency check, internal approval, electronic submission to the FSA / Local Finance Bureau, and public availability of the Art. 111 disclosure document

In-scope systems.value: Submission register and filing calendar; packages built from the financial reporting repository and lodged through the FSA electronic application and notification system, with receipts stored against the register entry

Compliance procedure documented.value: Annual FSA Submission Procedure (Japan) — package inventory, prescribed-form mapping, basic-documents consistency check, Art. 123 amendment trigger test, approval ladder, electronic lodgement and receipt capture

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the CFO and the General Counsel; re-approved whenever the Ordinance for Enforcement submission forms change or the supervising Local Finance Bureau changes the lodgement channel

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Business report and financial statements due within 3 months of the 31 March business year end (by 30 June); actuarial opinion submitted without delay after board presentation (internal service level 5 business days); Art. 111 disclosure document made publicly available within 4 months of business year end

Deadline reminders configured.value: Submission register alerts at 31 May (package assembled), 10 June (approvals complete), 20 June (lodgement window opens) and 28 June (escalate if not lodged), plus a board-date-driven alert for the opinion

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Submitted package as lodged, electronic receipt with timestamp and reference number, approval sign-offs and the basic-documents consistency check retained 10 years from the business year end

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Late lodgement, rejected or resubmitted packages, missing attachments and any operating practice found inconsistent with the filed basic documents are logged with disposition and remediation owner

Remediation sign-off captured.value: General Counsel signs off any resubmission, any late-filing explanation to the Bureau and every Art. 123 amendment triggered by a consistency failure

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every document lodged with the FSA / Local Finance Bureau for the business year — business report schedules, financial statements, actuarial opinion and attached report, solvency margin schedules and any Art. 123 amendment or notification

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on completeness and timing — a missing prescribed schedule, an unattached actuarial opinion, or lodgement after the 3-month statutory deadline is a fail; content differences between the lodged package and the ledger must be nil

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual per business year; the test runs once immediately after lodgement, with a mid-year readiness check on the basic-documents consistency register

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have prepared, approved or lodged any part of the submission package

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual submission assurance workpaper in the compliance evidence repository, linked to the submission register entry and the electronic receipt reference

Regulator-ready documentation.value: As-lodged package, receipt reference, approval trail and consistency check, producible for a Local Finance Bureau follow-up or an on-site inspection within 3 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Regulatory Reporting Manager is the named contact for Bureau queries on the submission; the Appointed Actuary answers opinion questions and General Counsel clears any answer conceding a filing defect

checklist.step: Build the submission inventory for the business year
actions: Open the submission register and create the business-year entry with due dates: business report and financial statements within 3 months of 31 March, actuarial opinion without delay after board presentation, Art. 111 disclosure within 4 months.
List every document the package must contain and the prescribed form it must follow, quoting the Ordinance for Enforcement form number for each.
Name an owner and an internal due date for each document — Controller for financial statements, Appointed Actuary for the opinion, Capital Management for solvency schedules.
Circulate the inventory to all named owners and get written acceptance of their due dates.
checklist.done: the register holds a complete, form-mapped inventory with a named owner and accepted internal due date for every document.

checklist.step: Confirm the lodgement channel and access with the supervising Bureau
actions: Confirm which Local Finance Bureau supervises the company and whether this year's package is lodged through the FSA electronic application and notification system or in paper to the Bureau counter.

Log in to the electronic system with the corporate account and check the account is active, the authorised submitter list is current, and the electronic certificate has not expired before the deadline.
Download the current submission form set and compare it against last year's forms, listing every changed or added schedule.
Record the channel, account status, certificate expiry and form-set version on the register entry.
checklist.done: the lodgement channel is confirmed, the submitting account and certificate are valid past the deadline, and form-set changes are listed.

checklist.step: Assemble the business report in the prescribed forms
actions: Populate each prescribed schedule of the business report — business overview, in-force and new business movements, insurance class results, policy reserve schedules, asset schedules — from the closed ledger and the valuation run of record.
Attach the cell-to-source map so every populated cell names its source system, report and line.
Run the internal completeness check that no prescribed schedule is left blank without the permitted 'not applicable' notation.
Hand the assembled report to the Regulatory Reporting Manager with the source map and a signed preparer statement.
checklist.done: every prescribed business report schedule is populated or properly marked not applicable, with a signed preparer statement and a complete source map.

checklist.step: Assemble the financial statements and the audit evidence
actions: Lock the 31 March statutory financial statements — balance sheet, statement of income, statement of changes in net assets and notes — after the close is signed.
Attach the independent auditor's report and the audit committee's report as required for the submission.
Reconcile the policy reserve, outstanding claims reserve and price fluctuation reserve lines in the statements to the valuation run and the reserve schedules in the business report.
Confirm no journal has been posted to the business year after the statements were locked; if one has, the package cannot be assembled until it is reflected everywhere.
checklist.done: locked financial statements with the auditor's report are delivered, and their reserve lines agree to the business report schedules with no post-lock journals outstanding.

checklist.step: Attach the Responsible Actuary opinion and its attached report
actions: Take the signed opinion and attached report from the evidence repository together with the certified board minute extract naming the presentation date.
Confirm the opinion is signed, dated on or after the board presentation, and carries the Responsible Actuary's membership number.
Diary the without-delay submission date as board presentation date plus 5 business days and set it as a hard milestone on the register entry.
Check the reserve figures quoted in the opinion agree to the business report schedules line for line before the package is closed.
checklist.done: the signed opinion and attached report are in the package, agree to the business report schedules, and have a diarised without-delay submission date.

checklist.step: Complete the solvency margin ratio schedules
actions: Compute the solvency margin numerator (capital, contingency reserve, price fluctuation reserve, unrealised gains and other admitted items) and the risk denominator on the FSA-notified factors.
Reconcile every numerator input to the locked financial statements and every reserve input to the valuation run of record.
Complete the prescribed solvency schedules including the single and consolidated bases where both are required.
Have the CFO review the ratio and any year-on-year movement above 20 percentage points before it enters the package.
checklist.done: solvency schedules are completed on notified factors, fully reconciled to the statements and the valuation run, and reviewed by the CFO.

checklist.step: Run the basic-documents consistency check
actions: Retrieve the four basic documents on file under IBA Art. 4(2): articles of incorporation, statement of business procedures, general policy conditions and statement of calculation methods.
Walk each material practice reflected in the package — products sold, business lines operated, reserve methods used, dividend allocation — against the corresponding clause of the basic documents.
Record for each practice whether it is supported, silent or contradicted; treat contradicted as a live Art. 4(2) breach requiring escalation, not a documentation gap.
Log the completed check on the register entry with the reviewer name and date.
checklist.done: every material practice in the package is mapped to a basic-documents clause and marked supported, silent or contradicted, with contradictions escalated.

checklist.step: Trigger any Art. 123 amendment the check has exposed
actions: For every practice marked silent or contradicted, decide with the business owner whether the practice stops or the basic document is amended.
Where amendment is chosen, determine under Art. 123 whether it requires FSA authorisation or notification, and prepare the amendment document with a clean and marked-up version.
Lodge the amendment with the supervising Bureau and record the reference and expected turnaround, holding the practice until authorisation where authorisation is required.
Record the decision, the lodgement reference and the interim control on the consistency check row.
checklist.done: every silent or contradicted practice has a documented stop-or-amend decision, with authorisation-required amendments lodged and the practice held until cleared.

checklist.step: Tie the whole package out before approval
actions: Cross-foot every schedule and confirm each total agrees to the locked financial statements, the valuation run of record and the solvency schedules.
Check every cross-reference between documents resolves — an opinion citing a schedule number that does not exist is a defect.
Confirm file formats, naming and attachment size limits match what the electronic system accepts, and that no document carries a DRAFT watermark.
Produce a one-page tie-out summary listing each document, its version, its page count and its preparer.
checklist.done: the package cross-foots, every cross-reference resolves, formats meet the portal's rules and a tie-out summary is produced.

checklist.step: Obtain the internal approvals before lodgement
actions: Review the tie-out summary, the solvency ratio, the actuarial opinion form and the consistency check outcome.
Sign the approval record for the financial content and the solvency schedules.
Obtain the General Counsel's approval for the legal content and for any Art. 123 amendment being lodged alongside.
Record both approvals with names and timestamps on the register entry — lodgement is blocked in the register until both are present.
checklist.done: CFO and General Counsel approvals are recorded with timestamps and the register releases the package for lodgement.

checklist.step: Lodge the package and capture the receipt
actions: Log in to the FSA electronic application and notification system as an authorised submitter and open a new submission for the business-year report.
Upload each document against its prescribed form slot, in the order listed in the inventory, and complete the submitter and contact fields.
Submit and immediately download the acknowledgement showing the reference number, the submission timestamp and the accepted document list.
Compare the accepted document list to the inventory and, if anything is missing, resubmit the same day rather than waiting for a Bureau query.
checklist.done: the package is lodged, the receipt reference and timestamp are captured, and the accepted document list matches the inventory.

checklist.step: Submit the actuarial opinion within the without-delay window
actions: Lodge the signed opinion and attached report under Art. 121(3) as soon as the board has received them, without waiting for the rest of the package if the board date falls earlier.
Record the elapsed business days from the board presentation date to the lodgement timestamp on the register entry.
Where the elapsed period exceeds 5 business days, raise an exception and record the cause before the register entry is closed.
Send the Appointed Actuary the receipt reference so the opinion file and the submission register agree.
checklist.done: the opinion is lodged with the elapsed days from board presentation recorded and any breach of the 5-business-day service level raised as an exception.

checklist.step: Publish the Art. 111 disclosure document
actions: Prepare the explanatory disclosure document covering the business and financial condition for the business year, drawn from the same locked statements.
Confirm it is made publicly available at the head office and branch offices and published on the corporate site within 4 months of the 31 March business year end.
Capture a dated screenshot of the published page and a signed confirmation from each office that the paper copy is available for inspection.
Record the publication date on the register entry alongside the submission receipt.
checklist.done: the disclosure document is publicly available at offices and online within 4 months of business year end, with dated evidence on the register.

checklist.step: Handle Bureau follow-up questions and any resubmission
actions: Log every Bureau question against the register entry with the date received, the question, the responsible owner and the date due.
Route valuation questions to the Appointed Actuary, accounting questions to the Controller and legal questions to Regulatory Counsel, keeping the single channel through Regulatory Reporting.
Have the General Counsel clear any answer that concedes an error or a defect in the lodged package before it is sent.
Where a resubmission is required, lodge the corrected document, capture the new receipt and record what changed and why.
checklist.done: every Bureau question is logged, routed, answered by its due date and, where a resubmission followed, the corrected receipt and change reason are recorded.

checklist.step: Close the register entry and retain the evidence
actions: File the as-lodged package, receipts, approval records, tie-out summary, consistency check and Bureau correspondence as one folder under the business year.
Apply the 10-year retention label and confirm the folder is searchable by business year, receipt reference and document type.
Mark the register entry closed only when every inventory line has a receipt reference and every Bureau question is answered.
Carry any open Art. 123 amendment forward into next year's register entry as an opening item.
checklist.done: the submission folder is retained for 10 years and the register entry is closed with a receipt against every inventory line.

testing.step: Build the population of documents lodged for the business year
actions: Export the submission register entry for the business year with every inventory line, owner, due date, lodgement timestamp and receipt reference.
Independently list the documents shown as accepted on the electronic system receipts and compare to the register inventory.
Add any Art. 123 amendment or notification lodged during the year as population rows.
Sign and date the population as complete before sampling.
testing.done: a signed population reconciles the register inventory to the receipts, including every amendment lodged in the year.

testing.step: Reconcile the lodged package to the ledger and the valuation run
actions: Take the as-lodged business report schedules and compare the reserve, asset and result totals to the locked statutory ledger balances.
Compare the same totals to the valuation run of record and the solvency schedules.
Investigate every difference and reject any explained only as a rounding or presentation choice without a documented rule.
Record the three-way reconciliation in the workpaper.
testing.done: the as-lodged schedules agree to the ledger, the valuation run and the solvency schedules, with all differences documented.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of schedules and cross-references
actions: Take 100% of the prescribed schedules that carry reserve or capital figures and 100% of the Art. 123 amendments.
Take a seeded random sample of 12 further schedules and 15 cross-references between documents.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample is reproducible.
Confirm the sample includes at least one schedule marked 'not applicable'.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all reserve and capital schedules, all amendments and a random selection of schedules and cross-references.

testing.step: Re-perform the prescribed-form mapping on the sample
actions: Download the Ordinance for Enforcement form set applicable to the business year from the FSA electronic system.
For each sampled schedule compare the lodged layout, line labels and required sub-analyses to the prescribed form, without relying on last year's package as the model.
Confirm every 'not applicable' notation is genuinely permitted by the form's instructions rather than used to hide missing data.
Capture the form instruction page relied on into the workpaper with the download date.
testing.done: every sampled schedule matches the current prescribed form and each 'not applicable' is permitted by the form instructions.

testing.step: Verify the actuarial opinion attachment and its timing
actions: Confirm the signed opinion and attached report appear on the receipt's accepted document list, not merely in the internal package folder.
Compare the opinion signature date to the certified board minute extract and the lodgement timestamp.
Recompute the elapsed business days from board presentation to lodgement and compare to the without-delay standard and the 5-business-day service level.
Compare the reserve figures inside the opinion to the lodged business report schedules line by line.
testing.done: the opinion is evidenced as lodged, its timing recomputed against the board date, and its figures agree to the lodged schedules.

testing.step: Re-perform the basic-documents consistency check on selected practices
actions: Select five practices reflected in the package — one product class sold, one reserve method, the dividend allocation basis, one business line operated and one distribution arrangement.
Read the corresponding clauses of the articles of incorporation, statement of business procedures, general policy conditions and statement of calculation methods as filed.
Reach an independent supported / silent / contradicted conclusion before reading the compliance team's check, then compare.
Treat any practice you find contradicted that the check marked supported as an Art. 4(2) exception with immediate escalation.
testing.done: five practices are independently assessed against the filed basic documents and every difference from the internal check is escalated.

testing.step: Test the timeliness of the statutory deadlines
actions: Take the 31 March business year end and compute the 3-month deadline for the business report and financial statements and the 4-month deadline for the Art. 111 disclosure document.
Compare each computed deadline to the actual lodgement timestamp and publication date evidence.
Check the intermediate internal milestones were met and, where they were not, whether the slippage was escalated at the time rather than after the fact.
Log any late item as a breach with the number of days late stated.
testing.done: each statutory deadline is recomputed from the business year end and compared to actual evidence, with days late stated for any breach.

testing.step: Trace the approval trail behind the lodgement
actions: Confirm the CFO and General Counsel approvals exist, are timestamped before the lodgement, and reference the same package version that was lodged.
Confirm the submitting user was on the authorised submitter list on the lodgement date.
Check that the register blocked lodgement until both approvals were present, and test one attempt if the control is system-enforced.
Capture the approval records and the submitter list into the workpaper.
testing.done: both approvals pre-date lodgement, reference the lodged version, and the submitter's authorisation on that date is evidenced.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the document, the requirement missed (Art. 4(2), Art. 121(3), the 3-month or 4-month deadline) and the impact.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list — form set not refreshed, owner missed internal due date, approval late, consistency check not performed, portal rejection — and an owner.
Set a remediation date ahead of the next business-year package assembly kick-off.
For late lodgement or a lodged package later found incomplete, open a self-report assessment with the General Counsel and record the decision.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and, where lodgement failed, a documented self-report decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the test
actions: Compute the completeness and timeliness exception counts against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared and approved none of the package, sign the workpaper with name and date.
Report the conclusion and any statutory deadline breach to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper against the submission register entry.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion and exception counts, is reported to the Audit Committee and filed against the register entry.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the asset adequacy / future cash-flow analysis documentation pack and the Art. 115 price fluctuation reserve calculation; the Chief Investment Officer owns the asset data and strategy assumptions feeding it

In-scope processes.value: Annual asset adequacy work at the 31 March business year end — price-variable asset classification and Art. 115 reserve accumulation, asset model point build, reinvestment strategy assumptions, and the multi-scenario asset-liability cash-flow projection that supports the reserve adequacy conclusion

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must be independent of both the actuarial projection team and the investment front office

Evidence location for test results.value: Asset adequacy and price fluctuation reserve test workpaper in the model governance repository, linked to the asset extract id and the projection run id

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Category mapping with rate citations, limit and drawdown workings, scenario assumption schedule and results, producible for an FSA on-site inspection of asset-side adequacy within 5 business days
