checklist.step: Extract the price-variable asset holdings at the valuation date
actions: Run the 31 March holdings extract from the investment book of record for every general account portfolio, excluding separate account assets backing variable contracts and listing them separately.
Include per holding: security identifier, issuer, asset category, currency, book value, market value, acquisition date, and realised and unrealised gain or loss for the business year.
Produce control totals by category (holding count, book value, market value) and sign them onto the asset extract control sheet.
Deliver the extract to the ALM actuary through the actuarial data landing zone and confirm the Controller's investment ledger balances agree to the extract book values.
checklist.done: a dated holdings extract with signed control totals is delivered and its book values agree to the investment ledger.

checklist.step: Map every holding to its Art. 115 reserve category
actions: Classify each holding into the price-variable categories the Enforcement Regulation names — domestic stocks, bonds, foreign-currency denominated assets and real estate — and mark non price-variable holdings as out of scope.
Handle the hard cases explicitly: investment trusts and funds are looked through to their underlying category, and structured holdings are classified on their dominant risk.
List every holding that is out of scope with the reason, so exclusion is a decision rather than an omission.
Have the Chief Investment Officer review and countersign the category mapping before it is used.
checklist.done: every holding carries a category or a reasoned out-of-scope note, look-through is applied to funds, and the mapping is countersigned by the CIO.

checklist.step: Refresh the accumulation rates and limits from the current regulation
actions: Open the Ordinance for Enforcement schedule for the price fluctuation reserve and read the accumulation rate for each category as it stands this business year — do not roll last year's rate table forward.

Record the rate per thousand of book value for each category (currently of the order of 1.5 per 1,000 for stocks, 0.2 per 1,000 for bonds and foreign-currency assets and 0.5 per 1,000 for real estate) with the provision reference beside it.
Record the accumulation limit for each category and the basis on which the limit is measured.
Save a dated capture of the schedule page as the evidence behind this year's calculation.
checklist.done: a dated rate and limit table for the business year exists with a provision reference and a source capture behind every figure.

checklist.step: Compute the year's price fluctuation reserve accumulation
actions: Apply each category's accumulation rate to the category's book value at 31 March and total the required accumulation for the business year.
Add the opening reserve balance by category and subtract any approved drawdown to derive the closing balance.
Show the calculation category by category so a reviewer can see rate, base, product and running balance on one line.
Have an actuarial analyst independently recompute the totals in a separate file and reconcile the two before the figure is released.
checklist.done: the accumulation is computed category by category, double-computed independently, and the closing balance is reconciled with no unexplained difference.

checklist.step: Test the closing balance against the prescribed limit
actions: Compare each category's closing balance to its prescribed accumulation limit.
Where the limit is reached, cap the accumulation and record the capped amount and the excess that was not accumulated.
Where the balance sits materially below the limit, confirm the full year's accumulation was actually taken rather than reduced by choice.
Write the limit test result into the calculation pack and flag any capped category for disclosure in the business report.
checklist.done: each category's closing balance is tested against its limit, caps are quantified and any capped category is flagged for disclosure.

checklist.step: Assess and document any drawdown of the reserve
actions: Obtain from the Controller the realised losses on price-variable assets for the business year, net of realised gains, by category.
Test whether the realised loss exceeds the threshold the regulation sets before a drawdown is permitted, and compute the maximum permitted drawdown.
Where a drawdown is proposed, document the qualifying loss event, the computation and the resulting balance, and approve it in writing before posting.
Reject any drawdown motivated by earnings management rather than a qualifying realised loss and record the rejection.
checklist.done: any drawdown is supported by a computed qualifying realised loss above the threshold, capped at the permitted amount and approved in writing before posting.

checklist.step: Post the price fluctuation reserve and reconcile it
actions: Post the accumulation and any drawdown to the mapped price fluctuation reserve liability account with the calculation pack attached to the journal.
Reconcile the posted closing balance to the calculation pack by category and to the prior-year closing balance plus movements.
Confirm with Capital Management that the same balance feeds the solvency margin numerator and is not double counted.
Freeze the account once agreed and record the journal reference on the calculation pack.
checklist.done: the posted balance equals the calculation pack by category, ties to prior year plus movement, and feeds the solvency numerator once.

checklist.step: Build the asset model points for the cash-flow projection
actions: Convert the holdings extract into asset model points carrying coupon, maturity, credit rating, call features, book yield and market value by portfolio.
Group holdings only where the grouping preserves duration, yield and credit distribution, and document the grouping rule.
Tie the model point book value and market value totals back to the signed extract control totals by category.
Save the model point file against the projection run id in the model governance repository.
checklist.done: asset model points tie to the signed extract control totals by category and the grouping rule is documented.

checklist.step: Agree the reinvestment and disinvestment strategy assumptions
actions: Set the reinvestment assumption by scenario: target asset mix, reinvestment yield curve source and spread by rating, and the maturity profile of new purchases.
Set the disinvestment rule for scenarios where cash flow turns negative — which assets are sold first and on what market value basis.
State the assumptions the strategy relies on that management could not actually deliver in stress, and remove or haircut them.
Sign the strategy assumption sheet jointly with the ALM actuary and date it before the runs start.
checklist.done: a dated, jointly signed strategy assumption sheet sets reinvestment and disinvestment rules per scenario with unrealistic actions removed.

checklist.step: Run the asset-liability cash-flow projections
actions: Run the base scenario and every required stress — sustained low yields, a parallel and a twist rate shock, a credit spread widening with downgrades and defaults, an equity fall for variable annuity guarantees, and elevated lapse on high-guarantee blocks.
Export for each scenario and each projection year the asset cash flows, liability cash flows, net cash position, projected reserve and projected solvency margin ratio.
Identify the first projection year in which any scenario runs a cash shortfall or breaches the sound-management solvency level and quantify the gap.
Lock the run and record run id, model version, asset extract id and scenario set version in the run register.
checklist.done: every required scenario is run and locked, with cash flow, reserve and solvency paths exported and any shortfall year quantified.

checklist.step: Draw the adequacy conclusion and the required management action
actions: Compare the projected liability cash flows against the projected asset cash flows scenario by scenario and state whether the assets held plus future premiums support the liabilities.
Where a scenario fails, quantify the additional policy reserve, contingency reserve or asset reallocation needed, and re-run to prove the action closes the gap.
Take the action proposal to the Chief Actuary and the CFO with the yen amount and the funding period.
Write the conclusion in terms that can be carried directly into the Responsible Actuary opinion.
checklist.done: an adequacy conclusion is written per scenario and every failing scenario has a quantified, re-run and approved management action.

checklist.step: Reconcile the pack to the financial statements and solvency return
actions: Agree the price fluctuation reserve, contingency reserve and policy reserve figures in the pack to the locked financial statements.
Agree the opening solvency margin ratio used in the projections to the ratio reported for the same date.
Confirm the asset values used in the projection agree to the balance sheet investment lines by category.
Record the reconciliation as an appendix to the documentation pack.
checklist.done: every reserve, asset and solvency figure in the pack agrees to the locked statements and the reported solvency ratio.

checklist.step: Run the independent model risk review of the pack
actions: Assign a reviewer independent of both the actuarial projection team and the investment front office.
Have the reviewer re-run one stress scenario from the assumption sheet and re-perform the Art. 115 calculation for two asset categories.
Log review points with severity and owner; block the pack's release while any high-severity point is open.
Record the reviewer name, date and conclusion against the projection run id.
checklist.done: an independent reviewer has re-run a scenario and re-performed two category calculations, with all high-severity points closed.

checklist.step: Present the results to the ALM and investment governance forum
actions: Table the scenario results, the adequacy conclusion and any required management action at the ALM committee with the Appointed Actuary present.
Record the committee's decision on each management action with an owner and an implementation date.
Escalate to the board any scenario in which the projected solvency margin ratio falls below the sound-management level.
Issue the minute extract into the documentation pack.
checklist.done: results and actions are minuted at the ALM committee with owners and dates, and any solvency breach scenario is escalated to the board.

checklist.step: Sign, register and retain the documentation pack
actions: Assemble the pack: asset extract and control totals, category mapping, rate and limit table with source captures, Art. 115 calculation, drawdown workings, asset model points, strategy assumptions, scenario results, adequacy conclusion, reconciliations, review record and committee minute.
Have the ALM actuary and the Appointed Actuary sign the pack and register it against the projection run id.
Apply the 10-year retention label and confirm searchability by business year, asset category and run id.
Hand the pack reference to the Appointed Actuary for the opinion file and to Regulatory Reporting for the business report.
checklist.done: a signed, complete pack is registered against the run id, retained for 10 years and referenced from the opinion and reporting files.

testing.step: Build the population of price-variable holdings and scenarios
actions: Independently extract the 31 March general account holdings from the investment book of record and compare the record count and book value to the signed extract control totals.
Add every holding the mapping marked out of scope as population rows so exclusions are tested rather than trusted.
List every scenario the procedure requires as a population row, marking those absent from the run register.
Sign and date the population before sampling.
testing.done: a signed population covers all holdings including out-of-scope exclusions and every required scenario, with omissions visible.

testing.step: Reconcile the asset population to the ledger and the balance sheet
actions: Compare the population book values by category to the investment ledger and to the balance sheet investment lines in the locked financial statements.
Confirm separate account assets backing variable contracts are excluded from the Art. 115 base and shown separately.
Explain every reconciling item by name — trade date versus settlement date, currency translation, accrued interest — and reject unexplained residuals.
Record the three-way reconciliation in the workpaper.
testing.done: holdings agree to the investment ledger and the balance sheet by category with all reconciling items named.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of holdings, entries and scenarios
actions: Take 100% of asset categories, 100% of drawdown entries and 100% of holdings classified by look-through or judgement.
Take a seeded random sample of 30 holdings across categories and 2 stress scenarios for re-execution.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and rule so the sample can be re-drawn.
Confirm the sample includes at least five holdings marked out of scope.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all categories, all drawdowns, judgement classifications, out-of-scope holdings and two scenarios.

testing.step: Re-perform the category mapping on the sampled holdings
actions: For each sampled holding read the security terms and independently assign the Art. 115 category before looking at the company mapping.
For funds and structured holdings apply look-through to the underlying assets and record the basis of the dominant-risk call.
Compare your conclusion to the mapping; any difference, including a right category cited to the wrong provision, is an exception.
For out-of-scope holdings confirm the reason stated is a regulatory basis rather than an administrative convenience.
testing.done: each sampled holding has an independent category conclusion, with look-through applied and every difference logged as an exception.

testing.step: Recompute the accumulation, the limit test and the closing balance
actions: Independently read the accumulation rate and limit for each category from the current Enforcement Regulation schedule and compare to the rate table used.
Recompute the accumulation as rate times category book value and the closing balance as opening plus accumulation less drawdown.
Compare each recomputed figure to the booked amount to the yen and investigate any difference before calling it rounding.
Re-perform the limit test and confirm any capped category was disclosed.
testing.done: rates, accumulation and closing balances recompute to the booked amounts to the yen and the limit test result is confirmed.

testing.step: Test the eligibility of every drawdown
actions: Pull the realised gains and losses on price-variable assets for the business year from the ledger by category.
Recompute the net realised loss and test it against the threshold the regulation requires before a drawdown is permitted.
Confirm the drawdown taken does not exceed the permitted maximum and that the written Chief Actuary approval pre-dates the posting.
Treat any drawdown taken without a qualifying loss as a reportable breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: every drawdown is supported by a recomputed qualifying realised loss, is within the permitted maximum and has a pre-dated approval.

testing.step: Re-execute sampled cash-flow scenarios from the assumption sheet
actions: Rebuild the sampled scenarios from the signed strategy assumption sheet and the asset model point file without copying the original run settings.
Compare asset cash flows, net cash position and projected solvency margin ratio year by year to the reported results.
Confirm the reinvestment and disinvestment rules actually applied in the run match the signed sheet, especially in the shortfall years.
Investigate any difference above 1% of projected net assets and identify whether the sheet or the run is wrong.
testing.done: sampled scenarios reproduce within 1% of projected net assets and the executed strategy rules match the signed assumption sheet.

testing.step: Trace the adequacy conclusion into the opinion and the reporting pack
actions: Compare the adequacy conclusion in the pack to the wording carried into the Responsible Actuary opinion and the attached report.
Confirm every management action committed at the ALM committee has an owner, a date and evidence that it started.
Check the price fluctuation reserve balance in the pack equals the amount in the business report and the solvency numerator.
Capture the traced pages into the workpaper.
testing.done: the adequacy conclusion, committed actions and reserve balances are consistent across the pack, the opinion and the reporting package.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the holding or scenario, the yen impact and whether Art. 115 accumulation, the limit, the drawdown condition or the analysis scope was breached.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list — stale rate table, mapping error, look-through not applied, unsupported drawdown, scenario omitted, strategy assumption not executed — and an owner.
Set a remediation date inside the half-year recalculation cycle.
For any under-accumulation, open an assessment with Regulatory Counsel on restatement and notification and record the decision.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, a yen impact, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and, for under-accumulation, a restatement decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the test
actions: Compute the exception counts against the to-the-yen recomputation threshold and the zero-tolerance categorisation, drawdown and scenario-completeness criteria.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, drawn from neither the actuarial projection team nor the front office, sign the workpaper with name and date.
Report the conclusion to the ALM committee and the Audit Committee and file the workpaper against the projection run id.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion and exception counts and is reported to the ALM and Audit Committees and filed against the run id.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the quarterly reserve-data reconciliation between the policy administration extract, the valuation model points and the ledger; the Reserving Actuary co-signs each quarter's pack

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IBA Art. 116 (policy reserve must cover in-force obligations), Art. 120 (Responsible Actuary's reliance on the data) and Art. 4 (valuation must follow the filed statement of calculation methods), re-read at each quarter end against the current Ordinance for Enforcement text

In-scope processes.value: Quarterly reconciliation at 30 June, 30 September, 31 December and 31 March of the in-force policy population, its financial attributes and the resulting policy reserve, across individual life, annuity, group and third-sector blocks including variable contracts

In-scope systems.value: Policy administration in-force is the source of record; extracts land in the enterprise data warehouse, feed the actuarial model point build, and the reserve output is reconciled to the general ledger

Compliance procedure documented.value: Quarterly Reserve Data Reconciliation Procedure — extract freeze, completeness and field-quality rules, four-way tie (policy admin, extract, model points, ledger), movement reconciliation, difference classification and correction-at-source rule

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Actuary and the Data Governance Lead; re-approved on any policy administration release that changes the extract layout or on any new product launch

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Reconciliation pack signed within 10 business days of each quarter end; the 31 March pack must be signed before the valuation is locked for the business report due 30 June

Deadline reminders configured.value: Quarter-end calendar alerts at extract freeze (quarter end + 2 business days), tie-out due (+6), difference clearance due (+8), pack sign-off (+10)

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Extract control sheets, data quality rule results, four-way tie-out, movement reconciliation, difference log with dispositions and the signed pack retained 10 years from the business year end

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Failed quality rules, unreconciled differences above tolerance, records dropped by the model point build and model-side workarounds used instead of source fixes are logged with owner and disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Chief Actuary approves carrying any unreconciled difference into the valuation and signs off every model-side workaround with an expiry date

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every quarter's in-force policy population by product and status, its extract, its model point build and the reserve posted to the ledger — plus the movement records (new business, terminations, alterations) between quarter ends

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Record counts must tie exactly between policy admin, extract and model points; financial totals must tie within 0.01% of the in-force value; any dropped or defaulted record and any difference carried without Chief Actuary approval is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is quarterly; the test runs each quarter on that quarter's pack, with the 31 March quarter tested in full depth including seriatim tracing

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside both the actuarial data team and policy administration operations

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly reserve data reconciliation test workpaper in the compliance evidence repository, indexed by quarter end and linked to the extract id and model point build id

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Four-way tie-out, movement reconciliation and difference log for each quarter, producible within 3 business days for an FSA inspection question on the integrity of the reserve data

Regulator response path.value: Data integrity questions are answered by the Data Quality Manager with the Reserving Actuary, routed through Regulatory Reporting; the Appointed Actuary is informed of any difference that could affect the opinion

checklist.step: Set the reconciliation scope and tolerances for the quarter
actions: Open the quarter's reconciliation control sheet and list every in-force block to be reconciled: individual life, individual annuity, group life, group annuity, third-sector riders and variable contracts.
For each block name the source system, the extract job, the model point build and the ledger accounts it must tie to.
State the tolerance for each tie — exact on record counts, 0.01% of in-force value on financial totals — and note that tolerance is not a licence to carry a known error.
Confirm with the Reserving Actuary that no product launched or migrated during the quarter is missing from the block list.
checklist.done: the control sheet lists every block with its source, extract, model build, ledger accounts and tolerance, confirmed complete by the Reserving Actuary.

checklist.step: Freeze and run the source extracts
actions: Freeze the policy administration reporting environment at the quarter-end position and record the freeze timestamp and the system's last processed batch id.

Run the valuation extract, the movement extract (new business, terminations, alterations) and the dividend and fund value extracts as one scheduled dependency chain so all share the same as-at position.
Capture the row counts and financial control totals emitted by each job into the extract control sheet.
Reject the run and re-execute if any job read data after the freeze timestamp — mixed as-at data cannot be reconciled.
checklist.done: all extracts run from a single frozen as-at position with row counts and control totals captured and no post-freeze reads.

checklist.step: Prove extract completeness against the source system counters
actions: Run the policy administration in-force count and sum assured report for the same quarter end directly in the source system, independently of the extract.
Compare the source counters to the extract control totals by product and status and list every difference in units.
Investigate each difference to a named cause — status codes excluded by the extract filter, contracts in suspense, pending reinstatements — and confirm the exclusion is intended.
Sign the completeness statement onto the extract control sheet.
checklist.done: extract totals are compared to independently produced source counters and every difference is traced to an intended, documented exclusion.

checklist.step: Run the field-level data quality rules
actions: Execute the valuation data rule set: mandatory fields populated (entry age, sex, issue date, term, premium term, sum assured), issue date before the valuation date, entry age within the plan's issue-age range, premium mode valid, rider codes mapped.
Execute the cross-field rules: paid-up contracts carry no future premium, annuities in payment carry an annuity amount, variable contracts carry a fund value and a guarantee type.
Produce the failure report by rule with counts and example policy numbers, ranked by financial exposure.
Route each failure to the Policy Admin Ops Lead for source correction and record the ticket reference on the rule row.
checklist.done: the full rule set has run, every failure is quantified, ranked by exposure and routed to policy administration with a ticket reference.

checklist.step: Reconcile the extract to the valuation model point build
actions: Compare the model point build output counts and totals (contracts, sum assured, annualised premium, account value) to the extract control totals by block.
Read the build log and list every record rejected, dropped or defaulted, with the reason code.
Confirm the defaulted-field counter is zero for entry age, sex, term and premium term; a default silently changes the reserve.
Record the extract-to-model-point tie on the control sheet with the build id.
checklist.done: model point totals tie to the extract by block with zero dropped or defaulted records, evidenced by the build log.

checklist.step: Reconcile the in-force movement from the prior quarter
actions: Build the movement bridge: prior quarter closing in-force plus new business and reinstatements, less deaths, surrenders, lapses, maturities, annuitisations and conversions, equals this quarter's closing in-force.
Reconcile each movement category count and amount to the movement extract and to the claims and policy service systems that generated it.
Investigate any bridge residual above 0.01% of in-force value and resolve it before the pack is signed rather than plugging the difference.
Present the bridge by block with the three largest movements narrated.
checklist.done: the movement bridge closes from prior to current quarter for every block with no residual above 0.01% and each category agreed to its source system.

checklist.step: Reconcile premium and billing data
actions: Compare the annualised premium in the extract to the billing system's in-force annualised premium by product and mode.
Reconcile the unearned premium base — modal premium and last premium due date — for a sample of blocks against billing records.
Investigate policies in the extract as premium-paying that the billing system shows as lapsed for non-payment, and the reverse.
Return the differences to Policy Admin Ops for correction at source and record the ticket references.
checklist.done: extract premium data agrees to the billing system by product and mode, with premium-status conflicts routed for source correction.

checklist.step: Reconcile variable contract fund values to the unit ledger
actions: Compare the account values on variable contracts in the extract to the separate account unit ledger at the same quarter-end unit price date.
Confirm units held times unit price equals the account value on the extract for every fund, and list any contract where it does not.
Check the guaranteed minimum benefit type and guarantee base on each contract against the product administration record, since these drive the minimum guarantee reserve.
Sign the fund value reconciliation onto the control sheet.
checklist.done: variable contract account values reconcile to units times unit price on the unit ledger and every guarantee type and base is confirmed.

checklist.step: Reconcile the reserve output to the general ledger
actions: Compare the reserve by component from the valuation run to the posted statutory liability account balances for the quarter.
Identify any top-side or manual journal posted to a reserve account outside the valuation run and require it to be supported by an actuarial memorandum.
Reconcile the reserve movement in the quarter to the movement bridge so the financial movement and the policy movement tell the same story.
Attach the reconciliation to the quarter's close file.
checklist.done: ledger reserve balances equal the valuation run by component, every manual journal is supported, and reserve movement agrees to the in-force movement bridge.

checklist.step: Classify every difference and set its disposition
actions: Log every unresolved difference with block, amount, tie point and the systems involved.
Classify each as source data defect, extract logic defect, model mapping defect, timing, or genuine business event, and name the owner.
Quantify the reserve effect of each difference so materiality is a number rather than an opinion.
Set a correction date; timing differences must reverse in the following quarter and are re-tested then.
checklist.done: every difference is logged, classified, quantified in reserve terms and given an owner and a correction date.

checklist.step: Correct at source rather than in the model
actions: Fix confirmed source data defects in the policy administration record, not in the extract or the model point file.
Where a fix cannot be made before the valuation lock, agree a model-side workaround in writing with the Reserving Actuary, state its reserve effect and give it an expiry date.
Register every workaround in the workaround log and review the log at the start of the next quarter.
Re-run the extract and the model point build after material source corrections rather than patching totals.
checklist.done: confirmed defects are corrected in policy administration and every model-side workaround is written, quantified, dated and registered.

checklist.step: Re-run and prove the four-way tie
actions: Re-execute the extract, the model point build and the valuation after corrections and record the new ids on the control sheet.
Prove the four-way tie in one table: policy administration source counters, extract, model points, ledger.
Confirm every previously open difference is either cleared or carried with an approval reference.
Lock the run that will be used for reporting and mark it as the quarter's run of record.
checklist.done: a single table proves the four-way tie for the quarter and the reporting run is locked and marked as the run of record.

checklist.step: Sign the quarterly reconciliation pack
actions: Review the four-way tie, the movement bridge, the data quality failure trend and the open difference log with its reserve effects.
Approve in writing any difference being carried into the valuation, stating the amount and why it is acceptable.
Sign the pack jointly with the Data Quality Manager and the Controller.
Release the pack to the Appointed Actuary, who relies on it when confirming reserve adequacy.
checklist.done: the pack is signed by the Chief Actuary, Data Quality Manager and Controller with every carried difference explicitly approved in writing.

checklist.step: Track the trend and drive the recurring defects out
actions: Publish the quarter's rule failure counts, difference counts and reserve effect alongside the previous four quarters.
Identify rules that fail every quarter and raise a permanent fix — validation at data entry, a policy administration configuration change, or a product setup correction.
Assign each recurring defect an owner in the owning operations team with a target quarter for elimination.
Report the trend to the data governance forum and record the decisions.
checklist.done: a five-quarter trend is published and every recurring defect has a named owner and a target quarter for permanent elimination.

checklist.step: Retain the pack and roll open items forward
actions: File the control sheet, extract control totals, rule results, four-way tie, movement bridge, difference log, workaround log and signatures as one folder for the quarter.
Apply the 10-year retention label and confirm searchability by quarter end, block and extract id.
Copy every open difference and unexpired workaround into next quarter's control sheet as opening items.
Confirm to the Appointed Actuary which open items remain outstanding ahead of the year-end opinion.
checklist.done: the quarter's pack is retained for 10 years and every open difference and workaround is carried into the next quarter's control sheet.

testing.step: Build the population of blocks, extracts and reconciliation ties
actions: Export the quarter's control sheet listing every block, extract id, model point build id and ledger account in scope.
Independently list the products in force from the product master and compare to the block list so a whole block cannot be missing.
Add every rule failure and open difference as population rows.
Sign and date the population before sampling.
testing.done: a signed population covers every in-force block from the product master, every tie point and every open difference.

testing.step: Reconcile the population back to the source system independently
actions: Run your own in-force count and sum assured query in policy administration at the quarter-end freeze point.
Compare it to the extract control totals and the model point totals without using the team's tie-out sheet.
Compare the reserve total to the posted ledger balances by component.
Explain every difference in units and reject any explained only as an extract filter without the filter definition attached.
testing.done: an independent four-way comparison reproduces the tie, with every difference explained by a documented filter or cause.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of policies and differences
actions: Take 100% of open differences and 100% of active model-side workarounds.
Take a seeded random sample of 40 policies spread across individual life, annuity, group and variable blocks for seriatim tracing.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and rule so the sample is reproducible.
Include at least five policies that changed status during the quarter so movement handling is tested.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all open differences, all workarounds and 40 policies including status changes.

testing.step: Trace sampled policies seriatim from source to model point
actions: Open each sampled policy in policy administration and read entry age, sex, issue date, term, premium term, sum assured, mode, rider codes and status directly from the contract screen.
Compare each field to the extract record and then to the model point, listing any transformation applied between them.
Confirm no field was defaulted or derived where the source held a value.
Capture the source screen for each sampled policy into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled policy's fields are traced source to extract to model point with every transformation identified and evidenced by a screen capture.

testing.step: Re-perform the movement bridge for one block
actions: Select the block with the largest reserve and rebuild the movement bridge from the prior quarter closing position using the movement extract.
Agree each movement category to the originating system — deaths to the claims platform, surrenders and maturities to policy service, new business to the issue register.
Compare your bridge to the team's and investigate any category difference above 0.01% of in-force value.
Confirm the reserve movement in the ledger for the same block is consistent with the policy movement.
testing.done: the independently rebuilt bridge closes for the selected block and agrees to the team's bridge and to the ledger reserve movement.

testing.step: Re-run the data quality rules and test the failure handling
actions: Re-execute the valuation rule set on the frozen extract and compare failure counts to the reported results.
Confirm every reported failure has a source correction ticket and check five tickets through to a corrected policy record.
Test whether any rule was disabled, weakened or excluded during the quarter and confirm the change was approved.
Look for failures that recur every quarter and confirm they appear on the recurring defect list with an owner.
testing.done: rule results reproduce, sampled failures trace to corrected records, and no rule was silently disabled or weakened.

testing.step: Test the disposition of carried differences and workarounds
actions: For each carried difference confirm a written Chief Actuary approval exists, pre-dates the valuation lock and states the amount.
Recompute the reserve effect quoted for each difference and compare to the stated amount.
For each model-side workaround confirm it has an expiry date, is registered, and has not been rolled forward beyond its expiry without re-approval.
Confirm timing differences flagged last quarter actually reversed this quarter.
testing.done: every carried difference has a pre-dated approval with a recomputed effect and no workaround has outlived its expiry without re-approval.

testing.step: Verify the ledger tie and the treatment of manual journals
actions: List every journal posted to a statutory reserve account in the quarter and separate valuation-generated postings from manual entries.
For each manual entry read the supporting actuarial memorandum and confirm it names the block, the amount and the reason.
Confirm the sum of valuation postings plus supported manual entries equals the closing reserve balance.
Flag any manual entry without a memorandum as an exception regardless of size.
testing.done: every reserve journal is classified and supported, and valuation plus supported manual entries equal the closing balance.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the block, the tie point that failed and the reserve effect in yen.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list — source data defect, extract filter, model mapping, unapproved workaround, unsupported journal, movement not captured — and an owner.
Set a remediation date inside the next quarterly cycle and mark any exception that would affect the year-end opinion for immediate escalation to the Appointed Actuary.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, a reserve effect, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the exact-count and 0.01% financial tolerances and the zero-tolerance dropped-record criterion.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, outside actuarial data and policy administration operations, sign the workpaper with name and date.
Report the conclusion to the Chief Actuary and the data governance forum and file the workpaper under the quarter end.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion and exception rate, is reported to the Chief Actuary and data governance forum, and is filed under the quarter end.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Responsible Actuary answers valuation and reserve questions personally, including explanation requests directed to the actuary under IBA Art. 122; the Regulatory Reporting Manager owns the channel, the clock and the register

In-scope processes.value: Event-driven handling of FSA and Local Finance Bureau valuation inquiries — supervisory questions on reserve levels and methods, price fluctuation reserve accumulation and drawdowns, on-site inspection questions and follow-ups to the Responsible Actuary opinion

In-scope systems.value: Regulatory inquiry register holds every request, deadline, owner, draft, approval and lodgement receipt; supporting workpapers are pulled from the compliance evidence repository under a preservation hold

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the General Counsel and the Chief Actuary; re-approved after every on-site inspection cycle and whenever the supervising Local Finance Bureau changes the contact protocol

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: The date stated in the request governs; where none is stated the internal standard is 10 business days for a written valuation question and same-day for an on-site inspection question, with an interim holding reply within 2 business days of receipt

Deadline reminders configured.value: Register alerts on receipt, at 50% of the response window, at 2 business days before the due date and on the due date, escalating to the Chief Actuary and General Counsel if the draft is not approved

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: The request as received, the register entry, drafts with review comments, the recomputation workpapers, legal clearance, the response as sent and the receipt, retained 10 years from the response date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Missed deadlines, answers sent outside the single channel, statements later found inaccurate and commitments made to the regulator without an internal owner are logged with disposition and escalation

Remediation sign-off captured.value: General Counsel signs off every correction sent to the regulator and every response that concedes a reserve or accumulation defect

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every valuation-related regulator request received in the period — written supervisory questions, Art. 122 explanation requests, inspection questions and follow-ups — together with every commitment made in the answers

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on timeliness and channel — a response after the stated or internal deadline, or sent by anyone other than the named channel, is a fail; every factual assertion must trace to a pre-existing workpaper or a documented recomputation

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have drafted, approved or sent any sampled response

checklist.step: Register the inquiry the day it arrives
actions: Create a register entry the same business day recording the receiving channel, the requesting office (FSA supervisory division or the supervising Local Finance Bureau), the named regulator contact, the date received and the date stated for reply.
Attach the request exactly as received, including the covering message and any attachment, without reformatting or summarising it.
Assign a unique inquiry reference and use it on every internal document and every page of the eventual reply.
Notify the Appointed Actuary, the Chief Actuary and the General Counsel within 4 hours of registration.
checklist.done: a register entry exists the same day with the request attached verbatim, a unique reference issued and the actuary, Chief Actuary and GC notified.

checklist.step: Classify the statutory basis and compute the deadline
actions: Determine what the request is made under — a supervisory report and materials request, an Art. 122 explanation from the Responsible Actuary, an inspection question, or informal supervisory dialogue.
Read the provision cited by the regulator, or the provision that fits if none is cited, and record the consequence of not replying.
Compute the response deadline from the date stated; where none is stated apply the internal standard of 10 business days for written valuation questions and record the computed date.
Write the classification and the computed deadline on the register entry — the answer's tone, formality and approval ladder follow from it.
checklist.done: the register entry records the statutory basis, the consequence of non-reply and a computed deadline date.

checklist.step: Send the acknowledgement and lock the single channel
actions: Send an acknowledgement to the regulator contact within 2 business days confirming receipt, the inquiry reference and the date the full reply will be provided.
Where the window is unworkable, ask for an extension in the acknowledgement with a reason and a proposed date rather than missing the date silently.
Instruct every internal recipient in writing that no one contacts the regulator on this matter except through the named channel, and that any inbound call is logged and referred.
Record the acknowledgement and any extension agreement on the register entry.
checklist.done: an acknowledgement is sent within 2 business days, any extension is agreed in writing, and the single-channel instruction is issued and recorded.

checklist.step: Break the request into discrete answerable items
actions: Split the request into numbered items, one per question or data demand, keeping the regulator's own numbering visible alongside.
For each item state exactly what is being asked — a figure, a method explanation, a document, or a justification — since these need different answers.
Assign an owner and an internal due date to each item, working back from the response deadline with 3 business days reserved for review and approval.
Flag items that could touch a defect or a restatement so legal is engaged on them from the start.
checklist.done: every question is a numbered item with a stated answer type, an owner, an internal due date and a legal-sensitivity flag.

checklist.step: Place a preservation hold on the underlying evidence
actions: Identify the valuation runs, reserve calculations, asset extracts, price fluctuation reserve workings and opinion files the request touches.
Apply a preservation hold so those records cannot be edited, superseded or purged while the inquiry is open.
Notify the actuarial, investment and finance owners in writing that the hold is in place and what it covers.
Record the held record ids on the register entry.
checklist.done: every record the inquiry touches is under a documented preservation hold with owners notified and ids listed on the register.

checklist.step: Retrieve the evidence behind each item
actions: For each item pull the specific workpaper, run output, rate table capture or reconciliation that answers it, down to the page.
Confirm the evidence is the version as at the date the regulator is asking about, not the current version.
Where no pre-existing evidence answers the item, record that gap explicitly — it is a control finding as well as a drafting problem.
Build an item-to-evidence map that will sit behind the reply.
checklist.done: each item has date-correct evidence identified to the page, and every item lacking evidence is recorded as a gap.

checklist.step: Recompute anything the regulator has questioned before answering
actions: Where the request questions a figure — a reserve level, an accumulation rate applied, a drawdown, an IBNR estimate — recompute it independently before defending it.
Compare the recomputation to the reported figure and, if they differ, treat the difference as the real answer and escalate immediately to the Chief Actuary and General Counsel.
Document the recomputation as a dated workpaper referenced from the reply.
Never assert a figure in a regulator reply that has not been re-derived or re-confirmed for this purpose.
checklist.done: every questioned figure has a dated recomputation workpaper and any difference from the reported figure is escalated before the reply is drafted.

checklist.step: Draft the reply item by item
actions: Answer each numbered item directly in its own section, stating the answer first and the supporting explanation after.
Cite the workpaper or attachment behind each factual assertion and attach the cited documents as numbered exhibits.
Where the honest answer is that a practice was deficient, say so plainly with the yen effect, the cause and the remediation with an owner and a date.
Remove speculation, hedging and any assertion that cannot be evidenced; an unsupported sentence in a regulator reply becomes a future finding.
checklist.done: a complete draft answers every numbered item with an exhibit reference behind each factual assertion and no unsupported statements.

checklist.step: Check the reply for consistency with everything already filed
actions: Compare every figure in the draft to the lodged business report schedules, the financial statements, the solvency return and the Responsible Actuary opinion for the same date.
Compare every method description to the filed statement of calculation methods and to the valuation report.
List each inconsistency and resolve it before the reply goes out — either the reply is wrong, or something already filed is.
Record the consistency check on the register entry with the documents compared.
checklist.done: every figure and method statement in the draft is reconciled to what has already been filed, with all inconsistencies resolved and recorded.

checklist.step: Obtain legal clearance on the reply
actions: Review the draft against the statutory basis to confirm it answers what was actually asked and does not volunteer beyond it without a reason.
Advise on any admission of a defect, its supervisory consequences and whether a business improvement response should be offered proactively.
Confirm that any commitment or undertaking in the reply is one the company can actually deliver, with an internal owner already named.
Record the clearance with reviewer and date in the matter file and attach it to the register entry.
checklist.done: legal clearance is recorded on the final wording, with every admission and commitment reviewed and deliverable.

checklist.step: Obtain the approvals the classification requires
actions: Route the cleared draft through the approval ladder set by the classification: Chief Actuary for valuation substance, CFO for financial figures, General Counsel for legal content.
For a reply that concedes a reserve defect or proposes a restatement, add the CEO and inform the Audit Committee chair before it is sent.
Record every approval with name and timestamp; the register blocks despatch until all required approvals are present.
Confirm the exhibits attached are the versions the approvers reviewed.
checklist.done: all required approvals are timestamped in the register and the despatch block is released against the exact approved version.

checklist.step: Send the reply and capture proof of delivery
actions: Send the reply through the channel the regulator specified — the FSA electronic application and notification system, the Bureau counter or the named supervisory contact — with the inquiry reference on every page.
Capture the submission receipt, timestamp and any reference number returned.
Compare the despatch date to the computed deadline and record whether it was met; a miss is logged as an exception even if the regulator says nothing.
File the as-sent reply and all exhibits against the register entry, locked against edit.
checklist.done: the reply is delivered through the specified channel with a captured receipt, and timeliness against the computed deadline is recorded.

checklist.step: Prepare the actuary for any follow-up meeting or inspection interview
actions: Build a briefing pack from the reply, the exhibits and the likely follow-up questions on method, data and judgement.
Rehearse the Responsible Actuary on the three answers most likely to be pressed, including the deficiency answers, with General Counsel present.
Agree who attends, who speaks to what, and that anything not known in the room is taken away and answered in writing through the register.
Record the meeting date, attendees, questions asked and commitments made as a file note within one business day of the meeting.
checklist.done: a briefing pack and rehearsal are completed before the meeting and a file note capturing questions and commitments is written within one business day after it.

checklist.step: Track every commitment made to the regulator
actions: Extract every commitment, undertaking and promised date from the reply and any meeting note, and raise a tracked action for each.
Assign an internal owner and a delivery date earlier than the date promised to the regulator.
Report open commitments monthly to the Chief Actuary and quarterly to the Audit Committee until each is closed with evidence.
Notify the regulator through the single channel if a promised date will slip, before it slips.
checklist.done: every commitment is a tracked action with an owner and an internal date ahead of the promised date, reported until closed with evidence.

checklist.step: Close the inquiry, learn from it and retain the file
actions: Close the register entry only when the regulator confirms satisfaction or the response period has clearly passed with no follow-up, and record which applies.
Record the root cause of the inquiry — a data gap, an unclear disclosure, a method the filed documents did not explain — and raise a control action to remove it.
Release the preservation hold only after closure and after the file is copied into the retained folder.
File the complete inquiry folder under the inquiry reference with a 10-year retention label and confirm searchability by regulator, subject and date.
checklist.done: the register entry is closed with a recorded root cause and control action, the hold is released after copying, and the folder is retained for 10 years.

testing.step: Build the population of valuation inquiries for the period
actions: Export every register entry classified as a valuation, reserve, price fluctuation reserve or actuarial inquiry with dates received, due, and responded.
Cross-check the register against the Regulatory Reporting mailbox, the General Counsel matter list and inspection file notes to find inquiries never registered.
Add unregistered inquiries to the population as automatic exceptions.
Sign and date the population before sampling.
testing.done: a signed population reconciles the register to the mailbox, legal matters and inspection notes, with unregistered inquiries flagged.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the regulator's own correspondence trail
actions: Read the correspondence thread for each inquiry and confirm every regulator message has a matching register entry and every company message has an approval record.
Identify any company reply sent outside the single channel and treat it as an exception regardless of content.
Confirm receipts exist for every despatch, not just the final one.
Record the reconciliation in the workpaper with message counts on both sides.
testing.done: the correspondence trail reconciles to the register in both directions, with off-channel messages identified.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of inquiries and commitments
actions: Take 100% of inquiries that conceded a defect, proposed a restatement or arose from an on-site inspection.
Take a seeded random sample of 8 further inquiries and 100% of open commitments made to the regulator.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample is reproducible.
Include at least one inquiry answered close to its deadline so the timeliness control is tested under pressure.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all defect-related and inspection inquiries, all open commitments and a random selection of the rest.

testing.step: Recompute the deadline and test timeliness for each sampled inquiry
actions: Read the request as received and independently determine the stated reply date or, where none is stated, apply the internal 10-business-day standard to the receipt date.
Compare your computed deadline to the one on the register and to the actual despatch timestamp, counting business days.
Confirm an acknowledgement went out within 2 business days and that any extension was agreed in writing before the original date passed.
Log any miss with the number of days late even where the regulator raised no complaint.
testing.done: each sampled deadline is independently recomputed, acknowledgement and extension evidence checked, and every miss quantified in days.

testing.step: Trace every factual assertion in sampled replies to evidence
actions: Take each numbered answer in the sampled reply and open the exhibit it cites, reading whether it supports the words used.
Confirm the exhibit is the version as at the date the regulator asked about, not a later restatement.
Where a figure was questioned, confirm a dated recomputation workpaper exists and pre-dates the reply.
Treat any assertion supported only by recollection or by a document created after the reply as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled assertion traces to a date-correct, pre-dated exhibit or recomputation, with unsupported assertions logged.

testing.step: Re-perform one questioned valuation figure independently
actions: Select the most material figure defended in the sampled replies — a reserve level, a price fluctuation reserve accumulation, or a drawdown amount.
Recompute it from the source data and the regulation in force at the relevant date, without using the company's recomputation file.
Compare to both the figure reported to the regulator and the figure originally booked.
Escalate any difference immediately rather than logging it as a routine exception, since the regulator holds the asserted number.
testing.done: the selected figure is independently recomputed and any difference from what was told to the regulator is escalated on discovery.

testing.step: Test the consistency of replies with what was already filed
actions: Compare figures in the sampled replies to the lodged business report schedules, financial statements, solvency return and Responsible Actuary opinion for the same date.
Compare method descriptions to the filed statement of calculation methods.
Flag any reply that describes a practice the basic documents do not support, since that creates an Art. 4(2) exposure on top of the original question.
Capture the compared pages into the workpaper.
testing.done: sampled replies are reconciled to all previously filed documents with any basic-documents exposure flagged.

testing.step: Test the approval trail and the commitment tracking
actions: Confirm each sampled reply carries the approvals its classification required, timestamped before despatch and against the version actually sent.
Confirm legal clearance exists on the final wording rather than an earlier draft.
For each commitment made to the regulator confirm a tracked action exists with an internal owner and an internal date ahead of the promised date.
Test three closed commitments through to the evidence of delivery.
testing.done: every sampled reply has a complete pre-despatch approval trail and every commitment has an owner, an internal date and, where closed, delivery evidence.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the inquiry reference, the failure (late, off-channel, unsupported assertion, missing approval, untracked commitment) and its supervisory risk.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list — intake not registered, owner missed internal date, evidence not retained, approval ladder bypassed — and an owner.
Set a remediation date inside the next quarter and, where a statement to the regulator was inaccurate, require a correction cleared by the General Counsel.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and, for inaccurate statements, a cleared correction.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the test
actions: Compute the timeliness and channel exception counts against the zero-tolerance threshold and the proportion of assertions traced to pre-dated evidence.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted, approved and sent none of the sampled replies, sign the workpaper with name and date.
Report the conclusion and any inaccurate statement to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper against the register entries tested.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion and exception counts, is reported to the Audit Committee and filed against the tested register entries.

In-scope processes.value: Per-change gate on any product, wording, process or system change that alters a customer-facing document — policy conditions booklets, applications, contract summary and cautionary information documents, cooling-off notices, claim decision and payment letters, lapse and reinstatement notices and dividend statements

In-scope systems.value: Correspondence templates and policy document assembly live in policy administration; the master form inventory and approved wording are held in the document management repository and served to the customer portal and agent channel

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the General Counsel and the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager; re-approved on any amendment to the general policy conditions or any FSA supervisory guideline change on information provision

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per change and pre-use — no revised document may be used before its approved effective date, and where the change amends the filed general policy conditions the Art. 123 amendment must be authorised or notified before first use, not after

Deadline reminders configured.value: Change record milestones at wording cleared (T-45 days to launch), Art. 123 lodged (T-40), template configured and render tested (T-20), training complete (T-10), old version withdrawn (launch date)

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Documents used before their effective date, wording inconsistent with the filed conditions, notices missing a required element and superseded versions still reachable in any channel are logged with customer impact and remediation owner

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Regulatory Counsel signs off every wording correction, every re-issue to affected customers and every decision that a variance does not require re-issue

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every customer-facing document version live in the period — policy conditions, applications, contract summary and cautionary information documents, statutory notices and system-generated letters — across print, PDF, portal and agent channels

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — a live document missing a required IBA notice element, differing from the filed general policy conditions, or in use before its approved effective date is a fail; every live version must appear in the form inventory with an approval reference

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per change and pre-use; the test runs on every change at the pre-launch gate and, in addition, as a full inventory sweep each half year

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have drafted, configured or approved any sampled document version
