checklist.step: Take in the change and open a document impact record
actions: Open a document impact record for any change that touches product features, benefit triggers, claim handling, premium or dividend mechanics, distribution channel or a servicing process.
Record the driver, the target launch date, the affected product codes and whether existing in-force customers are affected as well as new business.
Name the business sponsor and the Policy Forms Specialist who will own the document work.
Attach the approved change request so the document scope cannot drift from what was approved.
checklist.done: an impact record exists naming driver, launch date, affected products, in-force impact, sponsor and forms owner, with the change request attached.

checklist.step: Refresh the form and correspondence inventory for the affected products
actions: Pull the current inventory rows for the affected products: policy conditions booklet, application and declaration, contract summary and cautionary information documents, endorsement forms, and every system-generated letter template.
Confirm each row shows form number, edition date, owning system, channel, approval reference and effective date, and complete any row that does not.
Walk the correspondence template catalogue in policy administration to find letters that exist in the system but not in the inventory.
Baseline the inventory as the pre-change version so the after-state can be compared to it.
checklist.done: a baselined inventory covers every document and system letter for the affected products with no template present in the system but absent from the inventory.

checklist.step: Map each statutory notice requirement to the artifact that carries it
actions: List the Insurance Business Act information and notice duties that bite on these products: pre-contract information provision, cautionary information, cooling-off rights, policyholder protection corporation coverage, claim notification and payment-period wording driven by the Art. 117 outstanding claims duty, lapse and reinstatement warnings and dividend statements.
For each duty name the exact document and section that carries it today, or mark it unmapped.
Treat every unmapped duty as a finding to fix in this change rather than as a note for later.
Have Regulatory Counsel confirm the map is complete before drafting starts.
checklist.done: every applicable notice duty maps to a named document and section, with unmapped duties raised as findings and the map confirmed by counsel.

checklist.step: Draft the revised wording
actions: Draft the changed clauses and notice text, keeping the statutory concepts intact — the benefit trigger, the claim documentation required, the payment period, the customer's rights and how to exercise them.
Produce a redline against the current approved edition so every changed word is visible.
Check the plain-language rendering with the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager so a required disclosure is not made technically true but practically unreadable.
Record the reason for each change beside the redline so the rationale survives to the next review.
checklist.done: a redlined draft exists against the current approved edition with a recorded rationale for every changed clause and a readability review.

checklist.step: Check the draft against the filed general policy conditions
actions: Retrieve the general policy conditions as filed under IBA Art. 4(2)(iii) and compare the draft clause by clause.
Mark each change as within the filed conditions, an amendment to them, or contradicting them.

Check separately whether the change touches the statement of business procedures or the statement of calculation methods, for example where a benefit change alters the reserve basis under Art. 116 and Ordinance Art. 69.
Record the conclusion on the impact record; a contradiction stops the change until it is resolved.
checklist.done: every changed clause is classified against the filed basic documents and any contradiction blocks the change until resolved.

checklist.step: Lodge any Art. 123 amendment before first use
actions: Where the change amends a basic document, determine under Art. 123 whether FSA authorisation or notification applies and prepare the clean and marked-up versions.
Lodge with the supervising Local Finance Bureau, capture the receipt reference and record the expected turnaround on the impact record.
Set a hard release gate: where authorisation is required, no use of the new wording until authorisation is received, whatever the launch pressure.
Report the lodgement and expected clearance date to the product sponsor weekly until cleared.
checklist.done: any required amendment is lodged with a captured receipt and the launch is gated on authorisation where authorisation is required.

checklist.step: Rebuild the claim notification and payment-period wording
actions: Set out in the conditions and in the claim correspondence what the claimant must submit, when the payment period starts, how long the company has to pay, and what extends that period.
Align the wording with the operational reality in the claims platform, since the outstanding claims reserve under Art. 117 is built on the same trigger and payment-period logic.
Have the Claims Director / Manager confirm the stated periods are achievable and that the claims workflow measures the same clock.
Draft the letter that must go out when the payment period will be extended, including the reason and the revised expected date.
checklist.done: claim notification, payment-period and extension wording is consistent between the conditions, the claim letters and the claims workflow clock.

checklist.step: Rebuild the pre-contract and cooling-off documents
actions: Revise the contract summary and the cautionary information document so the changed product features, exclusions, surrender charge and guarantee limitations are stated where a customer will see them before signing.
Revise the cooling-off notice with the period, the start point, the method of exercise and the address it goes to, and confirm the stated period matches the products in scope.
Revise the policyholder protection corporation disclosure to state the coverage that actually applies to the product.
Have Regulatory Counsel confirm each of these is a standalone document a customer can act on without reading anything else.
checklist.done: the contract summary, cautionary information, cooling-off and protection corporation disclosures are revised, self-contained and counsel-confirmed.

checklist.step: Configure the templates in the issuing and correspondence systems
actions: Load the approved wording into the document assembly templates with the new form number and edition date printed in the footer of every page.
Set the effective date rule so the template is selected by contract date or event date, and confirm in-force customers keep the edition that applied to them.
Update the merge fields the new wording needs and check none resolves blank in the standard test cases.
Record the template ids, versions and the release ticket on the impact record.
checklist.done: templates carry the new form number, edition date and effective-date selection rule, with all merge fields resolving and the release ticket recorded.

checklist.step: Render test the documents across every channel
actions: Generate each document for a matrix of test cases: new business, in-force alteration, claim decision, lapse, reinstatement and dividend statement.
Check the output in print, PDF, customer portal and agent channel, confirming no clause is truncated, no page break splits a statutory notice and every page shows form number and edition date.
Verify a pre-effective-date case still produces the old edition and a post-effective-date case produces the new one.
Attach the rendered specimens to the impact record as the evidence of the pre-use test.
checklist.done: specimens for every test case and channel are generated, defect-free and attached, with effective-date selection proven in both directions.

checklist.step: Approve the documents and set the effective date
actions: Review the redline, the basic-documents classification, the Art. 123 receipt and the rendered specimens together.
Approve each document by form number and edition date, recording the approval reference and the effective date on the inventory row.
Confirm no effective date precedes the Art. 123 authorisation date where authorisation was required.
Release the change to production only after every affected document row carries an approval reference.
checklist.done: every affected document is approved by form number and edition with an effective date that follows any required authorisation.

checklist.step: Withdraw the superseded editions from every channel
actions: Mark superseded editions withdrawn in the repository with the withdrawal date and archive rather than delete them.
Remove them from the customer portal library, the agent portal, the print vendor's stock file and any marketing microsite, and confirm removal channel by channel.
Recall physical stock held at branches and by agents, and record the quantity returned or destroyed.
Search each channel for the old form number after withdrawal to prove nothing is still reachable.
checklist.done: superseded editions are withdrawn and archived, removed from every channel with a post-withdrawal search proving they are unreachable, and physical stock is accounted for.

checklist.step: Train the distribution and service teams on what changed
actions: Build a short module covering what changed, why, which customers see which edition, and how to answer the three questions the change will generate.
Assign it to the agent channel, the contact centre, policy service and claims with a completion deadline before the effective date.
Track completion by team and escalate incomplete teams to their manager 5 business days before launch.
Publish the change note and a specimen of each new document to the agent portal.
checklist.done: training is assigned and completed by every affected team before the effective date, with specimens published to the agent channel.

checklist.step: Publish the updated inventory and monitor early use
actions: Publish the post-change inventory version with form numbers, edition dates, effective dates, approval references and Art. 123 references.
Compare it line by line to the baselined pre-change inventory and confirm every difference was intended.
For the first two weeks after launch sample documents actually issued to customers and confirm the correct edition was produced.
Ask the Complaints Manager to flag any complaint mentioning the changed wording for immediate review.
checklist.done: the published inventory reconciles to the baseline with every difference intended, and post-launch sampling confirms the correct editions are reaching customers.

checklist.step: Retain the document change evidence
actions: File the impact record, requirement map, redlines, legal clearance, Art. 123 receipt, rendered specimens, approvals, withdrawal record and training completion as one folder under the change reference.
Apply a retention label of 10 years from the withdrawal date of the document, not from the change date, so a long-lived edition stays evidenced.
Confirm the folder is searchable by form number, edition date, product code and change reference.
Record the folder location on the inventory row for each affected document.
checklist.done: the change folder is retained for 10 years from document withdrawal and is retrievable from each affected inventory row.

testing.step: Build the population of live customer document versions
actions: Export the form inventory for every affected product with form number, edition date, effective date, channel and approval reference.
Independently list the correspondence templates active in policy administration and the documents published to the customer and agent portals.
Add any live template or published document absent from the inventory to the population as an automatic exception.
Sign and date the population before sampling.
testing.done: a signed population reconciles the inventory to the live templates and published documents, with unlisted items flagged.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the issued-document record
actions: Extract the log of documents actually generated to customers in the period with template id, edition date and generation date.
Compare the editions generated to the inventory's effective dates and list every generation of an edition outside its effective window.
Confirm in-force customers received the edition that applied to their contract rather than the newest one.
Record the reconciliation with counts by template.
testing.done: generated documents reconcile to the inventory's effective windows and every out-of-window generation is listed.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of documents and notice requirements
actions: Take 100% of documents changed in the period and 100% of documents carrying a cooling-off, protection corporation or claim payment-period notice.
Take a seeded random sample of 20 further live document versions across channels.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample is reproducible.
Include at least three system-generated letters as well as booklet-style documents.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers every changed document, every statutory notice carrier and a random selection of live versions and system letters.

testing.step: Re-perform the requirement-to-artifact mapping on the sample
actions: List independently the Insurance Business Act notice duties that apply to each sampled product before reading the company's map.
Read each sampled document and mark which duties it actually discharges and where in the text.
Compare to the company map; a duty the map claims is carried but the text does not discharge is an exception, as is a duty absent from both.
Capture the relevant document pages into the workpaper with the clause references.
testing.done: each sampled document is independently assessed against the applicable notice duties with every gap or mis-mapping logged.

testing.step: Compare sampled wording to the filed general policy conditions
actions: Retrieve the general policy conditions as filed and as authorised at the sampled document's effective date.
Compare the sampled document's benefit, exclusion, claim procedure and payment-period clauses to the filed text.
Treat any difference as an Art. 4(2) exposure and determine whether it favours or disadvantages the customer, since that drives the remediation.
Confirm any Art. 123 amendment relied on was authorised or notified before the document's effective date.
testing.done: sampled wording is compared clause by clause to the filed conditions in force at its effective date, with every difference classified and any amendment timing verified.

testing.step: Test the claim payment-period wording against operational reality
actions: Read the payment-period wording in the sampled conditions and claim letters and note the stated clock and the permitted extensions.
Pull 15 claims settled in the period and measure the actual elapsed days against the stated period using the same start point the wording defines.
Confirm extension letters were sent, with reason and revised date, in every case the period was exceeded.
Confirm the same trigger and period logic feeds the Art. 117 outstanding claims reserve estimate.
testing.done: actual claim durations are measured against the wording's own clock, extension letters are evidenced, and the reserve logic uses the same trigger.

testing.step: Prove superseded editions are unreachable
actions: Search the customer portal, the agent portal and the public site for each superseded form number and edition date.
Ask the print vendor for the current stock file and confirm withdrawn editions are not held or shipped.
Confirm the withdrawal record shows a date and a recall quantity for physical stock.
Treat any reachable superseded edition as a live exception with a customer impact assessment.
testing.done: no superseded edition is reachable in any digital channel or print stock, or every instance found is logged with a customer impact assessment.

testing.step: Test the pre-use gate and the approval trail
actions: For each changed document confirm the approval reference, the effective date and, where required, the Art. 123 authorisation date, and check the ordering of all three.
Confirm the rendered specimens attached pre-date the effective date and match the version in production.
Confirm training completion for the affected teams pre-dates the effective date.
Log any document used before approval or authorisation as a breach rather than an exception.
testing.done: for every changed document, approval, authorisation, specimen testing and training all pre-date first use, with any breach logged.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the form number, edition date, the notice duty or filed clause affected and the number of customers who received the defective version.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list — requirement not mapped, wording drifted from filed conditions, effective-date rule misconfigured, withdrawal incomplete, training late — and an owner.
Decide with Regulatory Counsel whether affected customers must be re-issued the correct document and record the decision and its reason either way.
Set a remediation date and carry the exception into the next half-year inventory sweep.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, an affected-customer count, a root cause, an owner, a re-issue decision and a remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the test
actions: Compute the exception counts against the zero-tolerance criteria for missing notice elements, wording variance from the filed conditions and pre-approval use.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted, configured and approved none of the sampled documents, sign the workpaper with name and date.
Report the conclusion and any customer re-issue programme to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper by change reference and form number.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion and exception counts, is reported to the Compliance Committee and filed by change reference and form number.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns event-triggered notice generation and despatch within the required timeframe and the completeness of the notice log; the Claims Director / Manager owns claim-side notices

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IBA Art. 117 with Ordinance for Enforcement Art. 73 (claims payable or likely to become payable, including incurred but not reported, which drives claim acknowledgement and payment-period notices), Art. 116 (policy reserve, which drives lapse, reinstatement and maturity notices) and the general policy conditions filed under Art. 4(2)(iii) that state each notice period

In-scope processes.value: Event-driven notice generation and delivery across the contract lifecycle — premium due and grace period, lapse and reinstatement, cooling-off acknowledgement, contract change confirmation, annual policy statement and dividend notice, maturity and annuitisation, claim acknowledgement, decision, payment and payment-period extension, and unclaimed benefit outreach

In-scope systems.value: Event triggers, template selection and the despatch queue run in policy administration; despatch images and proof of delivery are archived to the document repository and surfaced in the notice log

Compliance procedure documented.value: Statutory Notice Generation and Delivery Procedure — notice catalogue with trigger, clock start and deadline; daily queue monitoring; merge data validation; channel and consent rules; undeliverable handling; failure rework; breach escalation

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Operating Officer and the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager; re-approved on any policy administration release that changes triggers or templates and on any amendment to the filed policy conditions

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Each notice carries its own clock from the triggering event — grace period and lapse notices before the grace period expires, claim acknowledgement on receipt of the claim, claim decision and payment within the period stated in the filed conditions, and a written extension notice before that period runs out

Deadline reminders configured.value: The despatch queue ages every pending notice against its deadline with alerts at 50% of the window, at 1 business day remaining and on breach, escalating from the servicing supervisor to the Policy Admin Ops Lead to the COO

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Notice log entry, the rendered document image, the despatch and delivery evidence, undeliverable handling and any re-issue retained 10 years from the contract's termination or the claim's closure

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Notices generated late, not generated at all, sent to a known bad address or with a failed merge field are logged with the customer count, the days late and the remediation action

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every customer remediation arising from a missed or defective notice, including reinstatement of lapsed contracts caused by an unsent notice

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every notice-triggering event in the period — premium defaults, lapses, reinstatements, contract changes, maturities, annuitisations, claim receipts, claim decisions and payments — matched against the notices actually generated and despatched

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on missed notices — every triggering event must have a notice despatched within its own deadline; a notice with an unresolved merge field, sent to an address already flagged undeliverable, or despatched after the deadline is a fail regardless of customer harm

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven and continuous; the control is monitored daily on the queue and the assurance test runs monthly over that month's triggering events, with a deeper quarterly test on claim-side notices

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside policy administration operations and the claims servicing teams that generate the notices

Evidence location for test results.value: Monthly notice timeliness test workpaper in the compliance evidence repository, indexed by month and notice type and linked to the notice log entries sampled

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Notice log extract by type showing trigger date, deadline, despatch date and delivery evidence, with document images retrievable per policy within 2 business days for a market conduct review

Regulator response path.value: Notice delivery questions are answered by the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager through Regulatory Reporting; Regulatory Counsel clears any answer that concedes a population of customers did not receive a required notice

checklist.step: Maintain the notice catalogue with its triggers and clocks
actions: Hold one catalogue row per notice type recording the triggering event, the exact moment the clock starts, the deadline, the source of that deadline (filed policy conditions clause or statutory provision), the template id and the default channel.
Review the catalogue against the filed general policy conditions whenever the conditions change, and after every policy administration release.
Mark rows where the deadline is contractual rather than statutory, since these still bind but escalate differently.
Have the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager approve the catalogue version and date it.
checklist.done: an approved, dated catalogue holds trigger, clock start, deadline and source for every notice type and is reconciled to the current filed conditions.

checklist.step: Configure and verify the event triggers
actions: Map each catalogue row to the policy administration event that fires it — premium not received by due date plus grace, status change to lapsed, alteration completed, maturity date reached, claim received.
Verify in a test environment that each event actually fires the notice, including edge cases such as a policy that lapses and is reinstated in the same cycle.
Confirm the deadline calculation in the system uses the same clock start as the catalogue, not the batch date.
Record the configuration reference and test evidence against the catalogue row.
checklist.done: every catalogue row has a verified trigger configuration whose clock start matches the catalogue, evidenced by tested edge cases.

checklist.step: Monitor the despatch queue every business day
actions: Open the notice despatch queue each morning and review pending items aged against their individual deadlines, sorted by time remaining.
Work items with one business day or less remaining first and record why each is still pending.
Confirm the previous day's scheduled generation jobs all completed, and treat a job that did not run as a same-day incident, not a next-cycle catch-up.
Sign the daily queue review with the counts pending, breached and cleared.
checklist.done: a signed daily review exists showing pending, breached and cleared counts, with all jobs confirmed run and near-deadline items worked first.

checklist.step: Validate the merge data before documents are produced
actions: Run pre-generation rules over the pending queue: policyholder name and address present and not flagged undeliverable, amounts populated and non-negative, dates populated and consistent, and no template field left unmapped.
Divert failures to an exception queue rather than letting a document print with a blank or literal placeholder.
Route each failure to the servicing team with the policy number and the field that failed, and require correction the same day given the deadline is running.
Report the daily failure count and top failing fields to the Policy Admin Ops Lead.
checklist.done: no notice is produced with an unresolved merge field, and every diverted item is routed with the failing field named and worked the same day.

checklist.step: Apply the channel and delivery consent rules
actions: Check each customer's recorded delivery preference and consent for electronic delivery before selecting the channel.
Where consent is absent, withdrawn or the notice type requires paper under the filed conditions, produce paper and record why the electronic channel was not used.

For electronic delivery confirm the address on file has not bounced previously and that the portal notification is paired with the document, not a link alone where the conditions require the document.
Record the channel actually used on the notice log entry.
checklist.done: the channel used for each notice follows the recorded consent and the conditions' requirements, with the reason recorded whenever electronic delivery is not used.

checklist.step: Despatch and capture proof for the notice log
actions: Release the print file to the mail vendor or publish the electronic document, and capture the vendor's despatch confirmation file or the portal delivery event.
Archive the rendered document image against the policy number, notice type and despatch date.
Write the notice log entry: policy number, notice type, trigger date, deadline, generation date, despatch date, channel, document image reference and delivery evidence reference.
Reconcile the vendor's despatch confirmation count to the release count daily and chase any shortfall the same day.
checklist.done: every despatched notice has an archived image, a complete log entry and a vendor or portal delivery confirmation reconciled to the release count.

checklist.step: Work the generation and despatch failure queue
actions: Review generation errors, print vendor rejections and electronic bounce-backs at least twice each business day.
Reissue the notice through an alternative channel the same day where the deadline is close, rather than waiting for the root cause fix.
Raise an incident for any systemic failure — a template error, a broken trigger, a vendor file rejection — and record the affected policy population.
Confirm every failed item is either successfully reissued or logged as a breach with the customer count.
checklist.done: failures are worked twice daily, reissued through an alternative channel where the deadline is close, and every unresolved item is logged as a breach with a population count.

checklist.step: Handle undeliverable notices and trace the customer
actions: Flag the address as undeliverable on receipt of returned mail or a hard bounce and stop further sends to it, so the same failure is not repeated monthly.
Attempt trace in a documented order: telephone and email on file, the servicing agent, the payer's bank record and the group scheme administrator for group business.
Record every attempt with date, method and outcome, since a lapse driven by an undelivered notice will be judged on the effort made.
Where the customer is found, resend the outstanding notices and restart any period that depends on receipt.
checklist.done: undeliverable addresses are flagged and suppressed, trace attempts are documented in order, and found customers receive the outstanding notices with periods restarted.

checklist.step: Run the grace period and lapse notice sequence correctly
actions: For each unpaid premium confirm the grace period is calculated from the due date stated in the filed conditions and that the warning notice is despatched with enough of the grace period left for the customer to act.
Confirm the lapse notice states the lapse date, the surrender or paid-up value applied and the reinstatement route with its time limit.
Check that automatic premium loan or non-forfeiture provisions were applied before lapse where the contract provides them, and that the notice says which was applied.
Hold any lapse where the required notice was not evidenced as despatched, and refer it to the Compliance Manager before the status changes.
checklist.done: no contract lapses without an evidenced, in-time warning notice, and each lapse notice states the value applied and the reinstatement route.

checklist.step: Run the claim acknowledgement, decision and extension notices
actions: Send the acknowledgement on receipt of a claim, listing the documents still required and the date the payment period starts.
Track each claim against the payment period stated in the filed conditions and despatch the decision and payment advice within it.
Where the period cannot be met, despatch the written extension notice before the original period expires, stating the reason and the revised expected date.
Feed every open claim, including those only notified, into the Art. 117 outstanding claims reserve data so the reserve reflects claims likely to become payable.
checklist.done: every claim has an acknowledgement, an in-period decision or a pre-expiry extension notice, and all open claims flow into the outstanding claims reserve data.

checklist.step: Run the unclaimed and dormant benefit outreach
actions: Identify contracts with a matured, annuitised or otherwise payable benefit where no payment instruction has been received after the notice, and claims approved but unpaid.
Run the outreach sequence — letter, telephone, agent contact and, for older cases, an address trace — recording each attempt with date and outcome.
Confirm each unpaid amount remains reserved as an outstanding claim rather than being released because contact failed.
Report the ageing population and the recovery rate to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager monthly.
checklist.done: every payable-but-unpaid benefit has a documented outreach sequence, remains reserved, and appears in the monthly ageing report.

checklist.step: Reconcile triggering events to notices despatched
actions: Extract every triggering event for the month from policy administration and claims and left-join the notice log on policy number, notice type and trigger date.
List every event with no matching notice as a completeness gap and every match despatched after its deadline as a timeliness gap.
Investigate each gap to a cause and reissue the notice immediately where it is still meaningful to the customer.
Report gap counts by notice type with the trend over the last six months.
checklist.done: every triggering event for the month is matched to a notice, with completeness and timeliness gaps counted, caused and reissued where meaningful.

checklist.step: Escalate breaches and remediate affected customers
actions: Raise a compliance issue for every completeness gap and every timeliness gap beyond one business day, with the customer count and the potential detriment.
Decide the remediation: reissue the notice, restart the period, reinstate a contract lapsed without notice, or pay interest on a late claim payment.
Assess with Regulatory Counsel whether the population is large enough to require notification to the FSA or the supervising Bureau, and record the decision either way.
Sign off each remediation and confirm it was executed with evidence.
checklist.done: every gap has an issue, a customer count, an executed remediation with evidence, and a recorded decision on regulator notification.

checklist.step: Publish notice performance to operational governance
actions: Publish a monthly dashboard of notices due, despatched in time, despatched late and not despatched, split by notice type and channel.
Show undeliverable volumes, trace success rates and the ageing unclaimed benefit population alongside them.
Take any notice type failing more than the agreed threshold to the operations governance forum with an owner and a fix date.
Record the forum's decisions and carry unclosed items forward each month.
checklist.done: a monthly dashboard is published by notice type and channel, and every failing notice type has an owner and a fix date recorded in the forum minutes.

checklist.step: Retain the notice log and the document images
actions: Archive the notice log with its linked document images and delivery evidence under the policy number and the claim number.
Apply a retention label of 10 years from contract termination or claim closure so the evidence outlives the contract itself.
Confirm retrieval by policy number, notice type and date range returns the image and the delivery evidence together in one step.
Test the retrieval path twice a year with five randomly chosen historical notices.
checklist.done: notice log entries, images and delivery evidence are retained for 10 years past contract or claim closure and retrievable together, with the path tested twice yearly.

testing.step: Build the population of notice-triggering events for the month
actions: Extract from policy administration every premium default, grace expiry, lapse, reinstatement, alteration, maturity and annuitisation dated in the month.
Extract from the claims platform every claim received, decided and paid in the month.
Reconcile the event counts to the operational reports the servicing and claims teams publish, resolving differences before sampling.
Sign and date the event population as complete.
testing.done: a signed event population from both policy administration and claims reconciles to the published operational reports.

testing.step: Match the event population to the notice log
actions: Left-join the notice log to the event population on policy number, notice type and trigger date, so unmatched events surface rather than unmatched notices.
List every event with no notice as an automatic completeness exception with no judgement applied.
Compare each matched notice's despatch date to its catalogue deadline computed from the trigger date, not the batch date.
Quantify late notices in business days and group them by notice type.
testing.done: every event is matched or listed as a completeness exception, and every matched notice's timeliness is computed from its own trigger date.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of notices across types and channels
actions: Take 100% of lapse notices, claim payment-period extension notices and unclaimed benefit outreach cases.
Take a seeded random sample of 40 further notices spread across type, channel and servicing team.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and rule so the sample is reproducible.
Include at least five notices to addresses previously flagged undeliverable.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all lapse, extension and unclaimed cases plus a spread of other notices including previously undeliverable addresses.

testing.step: Recompute each sampled deadline from the filed conditions
actions: Open the general policy conditions applicable to each sampled contract at its effective date and read the notice period and the point the clock starts.
Recompute the deadline from the trigger date independently of the catalogue and the system.
Compare your deadline to the catalogue row and to the deadline the system applied; a difference means the catalogue or the configuration is wrong, which is worse than a single late notice.
Capture the conditions clause relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled deadline is recomputed from the filed conditions and any divergence from the catalogue or the system configuration is raised.

testing.step: Inspect the sampled documents for content and merge integrity
actions: Open the archived image for each sampled notice and confirm the correct template edition was used for the contract's effective date.
Check every merge field resolved — no blanks, no placeholder text, no truncated address — and that amounts and dates agree to the policy or claim record.
Confirm the notice states what the customer must do, by when, and how, where the notice type requires it.
Capture each inspected image into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled image uses the correct template edition with all merge fields resolved and agrees to the underlying policy or claim record.

testing.step: Verify despatch and delivery evidence for the sample
actions: For paper notices trace to the print vendor's despatch confirmation file for that release, checking the policy number appears.
For electronic notices trace to the portal delivery or email despatch event and confirm the recipient address matches the consent record.
Treat a notice marked despatched in the log with no vendor or portal evidence as not despatched.
Confirm notices sent to previously flagged undeliverable addresses were suppressed and handled through the trace process instead.
testing.done: every sampled notice has independent despatch or delivery evidence, and notices to flagged addresses were suppressed and traced.

testing.step: Test the claim notice sequence and the reserve linkage
actions: For 15 claims received in the month confirm the acknowledgement went out on receipt with the outstanding document list.
Measure the days from the payment-period start to the decision and payment and compare to the period in the filed conditions.
Where the period was exceeded confirm the extension notice pre-dates the expiry and states a reason and revised date.
Confirm every claim open at month end, including those only notified, appears in the outstanding claims reserve data under Art. 117.
testing.done: the claim notice sequence is evidenced for each sampled claim and every open claim appears in the outstanding claims reserve data.

testing.step: Test the lapse cases for notice-before-status-change
actions: For every lapse in the month confirm a grace warning notice and a lapse notice exist with despatch evidence, and that the warning left usable time within the grace period.
Confirm non-forfeiture or automatic premium loan provisions were applied where the contract provided them, and that the notice said which was applied.
List any contract lapsed without evidenced notice and quantify the customer detriment — lost cover, forfeited value, lost reinstatement window.
Confirm each such contract was referred for reinstatement consideration rather than left lapsed.
testing.done: every lapse has evidenced in-time notices and correct non-forfeiture treatment, or is quantified and referred for reinstatement.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the notice type, the number of customers affected, the days late and the detriment.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list — trigger not configured, job failure, merge failure, address quality, vendor rejection, manual queue not worked — and an owner.
Record the remediation executed for customers, including reinstatements, restarted periods and interest paid on late claim payments.
Set a remediation date and, where the affected population is significant, record the Regulatory Counsel decision on notifying the supervising Bureau.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, an affected-customer count, days late, a root cause, an owner, executed customer remediation and a notification decision where relevant.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the test
actions: Compute completeness and timeliness exception rates by notice type against the zero-tolerance criteria.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, from outside policy administration operations and claims servicing, sign the workpaper with name and date.
Report the conclusion, the trend against prior months and any customer remediation programme to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper under the month tested.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion and exception rates by notice type, is reported to the Compliance Committee with the trend, and is filed under the month tested.
